title: Integrasi Faktor Lingkungan, Sosial, dan Tata Kelola (ESG) dalam Manajemen Keuangan Perusahaan
summary: Integrasi faktor Lingkungan, Sosial, dan Tata Kelola (ESG) dalam manajemen keuangan perusahaan semakin dianggap sebagai elemen penting dalam perencanaan dan pengambilan keputusan finansial yang berkelanjutan. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis bagaimana perusahaan mengintegrasikan prinsip-prinsip ESG dalam manajemen keuangan mereka dan mengeksplorasi dampak penerapan ESG terhadap kinerja keuangan perusahaan. Dengan menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif berbasis studi kasus dan analisis konten, penelitian ini mengumpulkan data primer melalui wawancara mendalam dengan pengambil keputusan di sektor keuangan dan keberlanjutan, serta data sekunder dari laporan tahunan dan laporan keberlanjutan perusahaan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa faktor lingkungan, sosial, dan tata kelola secara signifikan mempengaruhi keputusan investasi, alokasi modal, serta pengelolaan risiko dalam perusahaan. Integrasi ESG memungkinkan perusahaan untuk mengurangi risiko jangka panjang terkait dengan perubahan regulasi lingkungan, konflik sosial, dan praktik tata kelola yang buruk. Selain itu, perusahaan yang mengimplementasikan kebijakan ESG yang kuat menunjukkan peningkatan efisiensi operasional dan dapat memperoleh akses yang lebih baik ke modal, meningkatkan reputasi, dan mengurangi biaya modal. Meskipun demikian, tantangan utama yang dihadapi adalah kurangnya standar konsisten dalam pengukuran dan pelaporan kinerja ESG, serta kesulitan dalam mengukur dampak langsung dari faktor ESG terhadap kinerja finansial jangka pendek. Penelitian ini memberikan wawasan mengenai pentingnya integrasi ESG dalam manajemen keuangan untuk menciptakan nilai jangka panjang yang berkelanjutan dan mengurangi ketidakpastian di pasar global.

title: ESG-ТРАНСФОРМАЦІЯ БАНКІВСЬКОГО СЕКТОРУ УКРАЇНИ: СУЧАСНІ ТЕНДЕНЦІЇ, ІНСТРУМЕНТИ ТА ПЕРСПЕКТИВИ РОЗВИТКУ
summary: The article examines the current state, key trends, and prospects of ESG transformation in Ukraine’s banking sector amid wartime challenges, economic instability, and deepening European integration. It is substantiated that the implementation of environmental, social, and governance principles is gradually shifting from a voluntary practice to an important element of banks’ strategic management, risk assessment, and long-term financial stability. The role of the National Bank of Ukraine in shaping the institutional environment for sustainable finance and integrating ESG factors into banking regulation and supervision is considered. The main instruments of ESG transformation are analyzed, including green finance, lending to sustainable development projects, ESG scoring, environmental and social risk assessment, non-financial reporting, responsible corporate governance, and digital technologies. The practical implementation of ESG approaches by leading Ukrainian banks is examined, and directions for their further development are outlined. It is established that the environmental component is developing most dynamically, particularly through the financing of energy efficiency, renewable energy, and economic recovery projects, while the social and governance components require further development. The main barriers to this process are identified, including insufficient regulatory clarity, limited availability of reliable ESG data, and the impact of wartime risks. Directions for improving ESG transformation in the banking sector are proposed, including harmonization of national regulation with EU requirements, development of unified approaches to ESG reporting and risk assessment, and expansion of green finance instruments. It is demonstrated that the systematic integration of ESG principles can become an important factor in enhancing the competitiveness of Ukrainian banks, strengthening the trust of investors and customers, and facilitating their integration into the European financial space. Particular attention is paid to the need to combine regulatory requirements, market mechanisms, and banks’ strategic initiatives to ensure the sustainable development of the financial sector.

title: Typology of Digital Transformations in Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises
summary: The article is devoted to the study of the problems of digital transformation of organizations. The key concepts and classifications are analyzed, highlighting D. Winter's approaches, the interpretative approach, the process approach, the OMI classification, the basic technology approach, technological intensity, and others. The typologization of digital changes in an organization makes it possible to understand the depth of the phenomenon of transformation itself, to identify the strengths and weaknesses of deterministic approaches. As the number of digital transformations in organizations increases and the associated cost of implementing digital technologies increases, the importance of a deep understanding of the nature of transformational changes increases. As part of the work, the author proposed a new typology of digital transformation that combines various classification features and is applicable in the context of dynamic transformations in the organization, which is typical for developing systems. A practical tool for implementing the proposed classification is the digital transformation matrix, which reveals the essence of frontal, structural and process changes in the implementation of digital initiatives. The combination of the control object with the type of technology used can form various types of dynamic changes. The research results have the potential to be used for practical business analysis purposes in the planning and implementation of complex digital change projects in organizations. Also, the main conclusions of the work can be applied for further scientific research of the phenomenon of digital transformation in all its diversity.

title: A Study on the Relationship Between the Digital Economy, Industrial Relocation, and Labor Migration
summary: Digitalized economy has been revamping the world industrial division of labor together with driving industrial relocation by geographical relocation of industries into digital restructuring of industries chains. Being one of the main factors influencing the process of industrial relocation, labor migration will undergo significant change in the patterns and determinants of migration. It is evident that digital tech alters the spatial logic of labor migration by reducing the cost of information and transactions as well as industrial relocations keep moving the regional labor force overtime due to the creation of job opportunities and the shifting nature of skill demands. The research suggests that the results of this study would help to enhance the digital infrastructure in the interior areas and improve the policies on talents in order to bring in skilled employees. Meanwhile, firms should embrace remote-work models to reduce unnecessary geographic moves. Crucially, targeted digital training is needed for low-skilled migrants, so they are not left behind. The present analysis offers empirical support to the concept that there are new features and processes of migration in a digital economy environment, offering a reference for formulating regional coordinated development strategies and labor market policies.

title: Disaggregating ESG Practices and Performance Outcomes: Empirical Evidence From the European Healthcare Industry
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines the associations between Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) practices and organizational performance in 283 European hospitals. Drawing on agency theory, stakeholder theory, and the resource‐based view, it analyses ESG indicators as accounting‐relevant information within the institutional context of European healthcare. Using 2021 ESG scores and 2023 accounting and operational outcomes from ORBIS, the study applies PLS‐SEM to examine operating cash flow, profitability (ROA/ROE), and operational efficiency. In the baseline PLS‐SEM model, aggregate ESG is positively associated with all three outcomes, but disaggregation reveals substantial heterogeneity. Governance is positively associated with each outcome, social practices are negatively associated with profitability and operational efficiency, and environmental practices show no significant associations. The study contributes by showing that aggregate ESG scores can obscure pillar‐specific mechanisms and theoretically expected time horizons. In European healthcare, governance displays more direct accounting relevance, whereas the potential benefits of social and environmental practices may be indirect, non‐financial, or deferred.

title: How data assetization enhances corporate ESG performance: a knowledge management perspective
summary: Purpose Data assetization, the process through which firms convert dispersed data into governable, reusable assets, differs from digital transformation, yet its implications for corporate sustainability remain poorly understood. The authors examine whether and how data assetization affects corporate environmental, social and governance (ESG) performance from a knowledge management perspective. Design/methodology/approach The authors construct a firm-level data assetization index from data-related laws and policy documents and firms’ annual reports using a neural-network-based word embedding method. Using data for Chinese A-share listed firms from 2011 to 2023, the authors estimate fixed-effects models and conduct two-stage mechanism tests. Findings Firms with greater data assetization exhibit better ESG performance. Knowledge acquisition, storage, sharing, and application are potential channels underlying this relationship. The positive effect is weaker for firms with higher Tobin’s Q or more government subsidies. Jointly pursuing data assetization and sustainable development may exert short-term pressure on financial performance. Practical implications Managers should build integrated data and knowledge management systems and embed data assets into ESG-related strategic decisions. Government departments should improve data asset standards, valuation rules, and disclosure mechanisms. Originality/value This study extends the knowledge-based view from the deployment of knowledge resources to their prior formation, theorizing data assetization as the process through which data become governable, reusable knowledge assets. It links this process to ESG performance through four knowledge management channels, distinguishes it from digital transformation, and extends research on data assetization beyond financial outcomes.

title: Two hands of green innovation: how digital social responsibility fuels circular economy practices and net-zero outcomes
summary: Purpose This study investigates how digital social responsibility contributes to sustainability transformation by examining its effects on green innovation, circular economy practices, and net-zero-based green performance. Drawing on Stakeholder Theory and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the study explores the mechanisms through which digitally enabled responsibility shapes innovation-based environmental outcomes. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research design is employed, using survey data collected from technology-based firms in Vietnam. Structural equation modeling is applied to test the proposed relationships among digital social responsibility, exploitative and exploratory green innovation, circular economy practices, and net-zero-based green performance. Findings The results indicate that digital social responsibility is positively associated with exploratory green innovation but not with exploitative green innovation. Exploratory green innovation is positively associated with circular economy practices, and both green innovation and circular economy practices are positively associated with net-zero-based green performance. In addition, digital social responsibility shows significant positive associations with both circular economy practices and net-zero-based green performance. Originality/value This study advances digital sustainability literature by redefining digital social responsibility as a digital sustainability orchestration capability that links stakeholder engagement with dynamic capability formation. It further reveals how digital social responsibility-driven exploratory innovation translates into circular-economy practices and net-zero-based green performance in emerging-economy technology firms, offering new process-level insights into the digital-enabled sustainability transformation.

title: Green Innovation Effects and Driving Factors of Urban Environmental Information Disclosure: Based on fsQCA and Complex Mediation Analysis
summary: Abstract Government environmental information disclosure (Pollution Information Transparency Index, PITI) is a critical step in the environmental management system. To investigate the key elements driving government environmental information disclosure in a complex environment, this study uses sample data from 120 prefecture-level cities in China and employs the Pollution Source Regulatory Information Transparency Index to measure this disclosure. Based on the push–pull–mooring model, it utilizes fuzzy set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) and a mixed mediating effect model to analyze the configurational pathways influenced by factors such as public environmental demands, regional environmental problems, fiscal pressure, government–enterprise relationships, the rule of law environment, and governmental environmental attentiveness that facilitate high levels of government environmental information disclosure (PITI). Furthermore, it examines the direct and indirect effects of these configurations on regional green innovation. The findings reveal that six push–pull–mooring factors yield four conditional configurations for government environmental information disclosure. Overall, high public environmental demands and low fiscal pressure are universal conditions that drive government environmental information disclosure. Additionally, the complex mediating effect analysis shows that all four configurations can directly promote regional green innovation and also indirectly enhance it by fostering PITI. This paper thoroughly explores the underlying mechanisms by which different configurational pathways influence regional green innovation and systematically analyzes the interactions among various factors, providing new insights for advancing governmental transparency and offering theoretical guidance and practical recommendations for promoting regional green development.

title: Digital Transformation and Operational Efficiency in Petroleum Enterprises: Mechanisms and Panel Evidence from Chinese A-Share-Listed Firms, 2008–2024
summary: Amid the rapid development of the digital economy and China’s carbon-peaking and carbon-neutrality goals, digital transformation has emerged as a critical pathway for petroleum enterprises to improve quality and efficiency. However, the mechanisms linking digital transformation to operational efficiency in the petroleum industry remain insufficiently understood. Using an unbalanced panel of 45 Chinese A-share-listed petroleum firms over the 2008–2024 period, this study examines the direct effect of digital transformation on operational efficiency, the mediating roles of factor-utilization efficiency and technological innovation capability, and the moderating effects of ownership and firm size. The results show that digital transformation is significantly and positively associated with operational efficiency. Among its dimensions, digital applications exert the strongest enabling effect, whereas the digital-achievements dimension may suppress operational efficiency in the short run. The relationship also operates through two mediation channels: technological innovation capability transmits the effect significantly for both efficiency measures, whereas factor-utilization efficiency transmits it significantly for total asset turnover only. By contrast, the moderating effects of ownership and firm size are not statistically significant in the current estimates: the interaction terms of digital transformation with state ownership and with firm size are insignificant for both efficiency measures. These findings clarify how digital transformation affects operational efficiency in petroleum enterprises and provide evidence for designing more effective digital transformation strategies in the energy sector.

title: The impact of avoiding the risks of electronic bank transfers on the sustainability of banking performance
summary: Iraq’s banking sector has undergone sustained digital transformation since 2003, marked by branch-network expansion, the introduction of electronic payment systems, and the adoption of financial technology (FinTech). This paper examines how the volume of electronic bank transfers relates to the macroeconomic conditions that govern the performance of Iraqi commercial banks. Series published by the Central Bank of Iraq and the Central Statistical Organisation for 2011–2022 are analysed with Johansen cointegration tests, a vector error correction model (VECM), and impulse response functions. Electronic transfers cointegrate with interest rates, exchange rates, inflation, and gross domestic product (GDP). In the long-run levels regression, the interest rate enters negatively, whereas the exchange rate, inflation, and GDP enter positively. The error-correction term is statistically significant and corrects approximately 4.6 percent of a deviation from long-run equilibrium in each period, so adjustment proceeds slowly. Short-run variation in transfer volumes tracks the policy interest rates, while GDP contributes no significant short-run effect. The findings locate the growth of electronic transfers within the macroeconomic constraints of a post-conflict banking system.

title: Blind Box Cultural Marketing Strategies in the Digital Economy: A Case Study of POP MART
summary: Digital platforms have changed how people search for products, talk about brands and share their purchases. In the trendy toy market, this change is especially visible because buying a figure can involve character stories, online discussion and offline experience at the same time. This study examines POP MART as a case of blind box cultural marketing in the digital economy. A qualitative case study and literature analysis are used, drawing on academic research, POP MART's 2025 annual report and documented marketing practices. The analysis focuses on three dimensions: cultural marketing and brand value, digital platforms and consumer participation, and blind box consumption experience and brand loyalty. The findings suggest that POP MART builds value through character IP, keeps these characters visible through digital content and consumer sharing, and extends the blind box experience through collecting, communities and physical spaces. Although the blind box remains important, long term IP development and cultural adaptation appear more important for the future of the brand. The case may also be useful for other cultural consumption brands trying to build lasting consumer relationships.

title: Automated Validation of Service-Oriented and API-Based Enterprise Systems for Reliable Digital Transformation in Saudi Arabia
summary: The extent to which Saudi Arabia is undergoing a digital transformation now relies on enterprise platforms that are put together using APIs, service-oriented components, microservices, identity services, data stores, and capabilities that are managed externally. This architectural modularity speeds up the delivery process but at the same time spreads out any potential failures across the interface contracts, the parameter dependencies, the workflow state, the data semantics, the performance, the security, and the runtime operations. A service may therefore pass local tests yet the entire public or enterprise transaction end-to-end will still be unreliable. This review brings together recent evidence on automated validation methods that have been published between 2020 and 2025 and presents an integrated assurance framework aimed at achieving reliable digital transformation in Saudi Arabia. The review looks at specification-driven API testing, dependency-aware test generation, contract testing, cross-service functional and robustness testing, performance verification, security testing, and observability. Thirty peer-reviewed sources, verified by DOI, were chosen as part of a protocol-led evidence review with a focus on automation, architectural relevance, empirical support, and suitability for use in enterprise systems. The synthesis indicates that no one test technique offers enough assurance for distributed digital services; reliability instead comes from a layered body of evidence that links interface correctness with stateful workflows, service interoperability, resilience in the face of failure, security controls, and production telemetry. The paper suggests a seven-stage automated validation architecture and a continuous-assurance maturity pathway which transform diverse evidence into clear decisions regarding releases and governance. For Saudi organisations, the framework stresses interoperability, service continuity, auditable changes, and evidence-based risk control, thus connecting software engineering practice with the level of operational reliability required by national digital transformation programmes.

title: Impact in 2025
summary: The Consortium of European Social Science Data Archives (CESSDA ERIC) is a distributed research infrastructure that operates through a network of 22 Service Providers and 12 partners across Europe. In 2025, the consortium worked collectively to deliver on its strategic priorities: Data, People, and Landscape. It preserved, curated, and archived 46,000 primary digital objects, including datasets, that were downloaded or viewed 793,000 times. title: Preventing recurring material misstatements through behavioural sustainment: a 5S-based conceptual framework for financial reporting
summary: Purpose This paper develops a conceptual framework to explain how behavioural discipline is sustained in routine financial reporting work and how such sustainment conditions the recurrence of material misstatements under conditions of reasonable assurance. Rather than treating reporting reliability as an outcome optimised through technical rules or ex post detection, the paper reconceptualises financial reporting as a behaviourally enacted process shaped by routines, accountability, and reinforcement over time. Design/methodology/approach The paper adopts a structured conceptual integration of accounting, management control and behavioural literature. The 5S principles – Sort, Set in Order, Shine, Standardise and Sustain – are reinterpreted as a behavioural process framework that explicates how reporting routines are enacted, coordinated, scrutinised and reinforced across reporting cycles. The approach is conceptual in nature and does not constitute a systematic review or a design science intervention. Findings The framework suggests that the recurrence of material misstatements is shaped less by the presence of additional procedures than by the extent to which disciplined reporting practices are behaviourally sustained over time. It explicates how 5S operates through behavioural mechanisms – such as selective attention to materiality, anticipatory coordination, anomaly questioning, accountable judgement and reinforcement across cycles – that condition how formal reporting requirements are enacted in practice, without assuming the elimination of judgement or error. Research limitations/implications As a conceptual paper, the framework does not provide empirical evidence of effectiveness and is developed primarily from literature grounded in regulated reporting environments. Practical implications The paper offers accountants, auditors, boards and regulators a conceptual lens for interpreting whether reporting routines are behaviourally sustained or have become symbolic, without implying a prescriptive intervention. Originality/value The paper reframes misstatement prevention as a problem of behavioural sustainment rather than technical optimisation, enabling recurring reporting failures to be analysed as manifestations of instability in routine enactment rather than isolated procedural deficiencies.

title: Capital Market Pricing of Audit Quality Attributes
summary: Audit quality is widely regarded as a crucial external governance mechanism that impacts firms' capital costs. However, there is still limited evidence on the economic consequences of different audit quality attributes. Drawing on the information intermediary and signalling role of auditing, this study examines how audit quality attributes influence firms' cost of capital. Using panel data from Chinese A-share listed firms between 2018 and 2023, this study employs a two-way fixed effects model to examine five audit quality attributes: auditor size, industry specialization, auditor change, audit tenure, and audit opinion. The results show that auditor size and industry specialists are associated with lower cost of capital, but their effects differ across financing markets. This study extends the literature on the economic consequences of audit quality and provides practical insights for firms and regulators in emerging markets.

title: Digital transformation and workforce resilience in social enterprises: governance for crisis readiness
summary: Purpose This study examines how digital transformation, workforce resilience and governance integration influence crisis readiness in social enterprises. It explores capability-building as a potential mechanism connecting digital transformation and governance with crisis readiness, while governance maturity and ecosystem collaboration are considered contextual conditions that may shape these relationships. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative design combined a comprehensive literature review of forty peer-reviewed studies with six semi-structured interviews involving governance, workforce and digital transformation leaders. Inductive coding identified three themes: governance for crisis readiness, digital transformation enablers and workforce resilience routines, interpreted through institutional theory and dynamic capability theory. Findings Governance embedded in digital workflows strengthens reliability and accountability. Capability-building routines such as micro-drills, peer learning, and digital literacy translate strategy into continuity outcomes. Ecosystem partnerships and institutional maturity amplify these effects by improving interoperability, resource sharing and collective learning. Practical implications Integrating governance controls within digital systems and aligning workforce development with feedback and monitoring enhances readiness, transparency and long-term sustainability. Originality/value This study develops a mechanism-informed conceptual framework that integrates governance maturity, digital transformation and workforce capability to explain potential pathways toward crisis readiness in social enterprises. It identifies capability-building as a proposed explanatory mechanism and ecosystem conditions as contextual influences, offering an integrative foundation for future empirical testing.

title: Pengaruh Pengungkapan Sustainability Report, Green Accounting, dan Green Strategy Terhadap Kualitas Laporan Keuangan
summary: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh Sustainability Report, Green Accounting, dan Green Strategy terhadap Kualitas Laporan Keuangan pada perusahaan sub sektor farmasi yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia periode 2020-2024. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan data sekunder yang diperoleh dari situs resmi Bursa Efek Indonesia (BEI) dan website masing-masing perusahaan. Sampel penelitian dipilih menggunakan metode purposive sampling, sehingga diperoleh 16 perusahaan dengan jumlah observasi sebanyak 80 data selama periode penelitian. Analisis data dilakukan menggunakan analisis regresi linear berganda untuk menguji pengaruh masing-masing variabel independen terhadap Kualitas Laporan Keuangan, baik secara parsial maupun simultan. Pengukuran Sustainability Report mengacu pada pedoman Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) Standards yang mencakup aspek ekonomi, sosial, dan lingkungan. Green Accounting menggambarkan penerapan akuntansi yang mempertimbangkan aspek lingkungan dalam aktivitas perusahaan, sedangkan Green Strategy mencerminkan strategi perusahaan dalam mengintegrasikan aspek lingkungan dan keberlanjutan ke dalam kegiatan bisnis. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Sustainability Report berpengaruh negatif dan signifikan terhadap Kualitas Laporan Keuangan. summary: This study analyzes the relationship between digitalization, structural transformation, and carbon emission intensity in six ASEAN countries, namely Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, the Philippines, Vietnam, and Cambodia. The study uses annual panel data for the period 2004–2024, with the main estimation period covering 2010–2024. Carbon emission intensity is used as the dependent variable, while the number of internet users, industry value added, urban population, GDP per capita, international trade, and services sector value added are used as independent variables. All variables are transformed into natural logarithms so that the coefficients can be interpreted as elasticities. Estimation is conducted using the Fixed Effects Model with period fixed effects and Panel EGLS with period weights following model selection tests. The results show that digitalization, proxied by the number of internet users, has a positive but statistically insignificant relationship with carbon emission intensity. In contrast, industry value added, urban population, GDP per capita, and international trade have positive and significant relationships. Services sector value added has a negative and significant relationship with carbon emission intensity. These findings indicate that structural transformation toward the services sector is associated with lower emission intensity, while industrial expansion, urbanization, economic growth, and trade are associated with increased carbon emission intensity in the countries examined.

title: Geography-Based Funding and the Fintech Securities Crowdfunding Ecosystem in Indonesia: A Mixed-Method Analysis
summary: Background: The Fintech Securities Crowdfunding (SCF) industry in Indonesia has shown rapid growth, yet it faces challenges regarding the uneven distribution of funding access and the maturity of its ecosystem. While funding is a primary driver, the geographical dimension in an archipelago nation remains a critical, under-researched variable. Objective: This study aims to analyze the influence of Funding on the Fintech SCF Ecosystem and examine the mediating role of Geography in this relationship. Methods: This research employs a mixed-method approach. The quantitative phase utilizes Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) to analyze data from SCF investors. The qualitative phase employs Social Network Analysis (SNA) to map the relationships among ecosystem actors. Results: Quantitative results indicate that Funding has a significant positive effect on the SCF Ecosystem (t-statistic 2.938). Crucially, Geography significantly mediates this relationship (t-statistic 2.269), suggesting that funding effectiveness relies on spatial distribution. SNA results visualize the central role of platforms in bridging geographical gaps between issuers and investors. Conclusion: A robust SCF ecosystem depends not only on capital volume but on how funding strategies address geographical disparities. This study integrates the functional area of funding with geographical disparity theories within the Fintech Ecosystem framework, offering a novel perspective on "hyper-local" strategies for national inclusivity.

title: INTERNATIONAL PRACTICE OF CORPORATE FINANCE ORGANIZATION: FINANCING STRUCTURE, CORPORATE GOVERNANCE REFORMS AND STATE ASSET MANAGEMENT EXPERIENCE
summary: The article provides a comparative analysis of how corporate finance is organized in developed and emerging economies and draws practical lessons for Uzbekistan. The aim of the study is to identify which elements of foreign practice in the areas of corporate financing structure, corporate governance and state asset management are suitable for national conditions. The methodology combines comparative institutional analysis, analysis of World Bank statistical data and case studies. The sample includes the USA, Germany, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan. The results reveal substantial differences in the structure of national financial systems. In the USA, stock market capitalization exceeds domestic credit to the private sector by 1.17 times, whereas this ratio is 0.74 in Germany and 0.49 in Uzbekistan. In Uzbekistan, domestic credit to the private sector amounts to 32.8% of GDP and market capitalization to 16.1% of GDP, indicating that corporate financing is constrained through both the bank and the market channels. Among recent foreign reforms, the initiative on management conscious of the cost of capital and stock price launched in Japan in 2023 stands out: more than 90% of Prime Market companies have disclosed relevant plans, and their average P/B ratio has increased from 1.1 to 1.4. South Korea's 2024 Value-up programme follows the same logic. Kazakhstan's People's IPO and Singapore's Temasek model are shown to be effective ways of subjecting state assets to market discipline. At the same time, because stock market liquidity in Uzbekistan is low and most shares are owned by the state, exchange-led initiatives need to be combined with the state's requirements as an owner. The article proposes forming a mixed financing model, transferring state-owned enterprises to professional management, introducing cost-of-capital-oriented disclosure requirements and clearly defining dividend policy in legislation.

title: Peer Pressure in Green Innovation: Green Innovation or Greenwashing?
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines whether a firm engages in green innovation or greenwashing in response to pressure from its business rivals' engagement in green innovation. Using a sample of 2958 firm‐year observations from 720 US publicly listed firms from 2010 to 2023, we find that a gap in green innovation between a focal firm and its top business rivals is significantly and positively associated with the focal firm's greater greenwashing but not green innovation. This effect is more pronounced when the firm is financially constrained, operates in a non‐carbon‐intensive industry, or faces stronger product market competition. These findings provide new insights for investors, policymakers, and scholars into the externalities, showing that rival firms' positive environmental initiatives may generate negative spillovers when focal firms respond opportunistically.

title: Digital Transformation and Systemic Risk in Chinese Commercial Banks: Dynamic and Conditional-Effect Analyses
summary: Using an unbalanced panel of 200 Chinese commercial banks over 2010–2021, this study measures systemic risk using market-based marginal expected shortfall (MES) for listed banks and SVM-completed MES for non-listed banks. Two-way fixed-effects, distributed-lag, conditional-effect, heterogeneity, and endogeneity analyses indicate that overall digital transformation is associated with lower systemic risk. Strategic and management digitalization reduce risk, whereas business digitalization is associated with contemporaneous adjustment pressure. The negative effect of overall transformation emerges mainly in later periods, is stronger for banks with greater asset-side risk-bearing capacity, stronger interbank funding dependence, and lower profitability, and is more pronounced among nationwide banks than regional banks. The findings clarify how digital transformation can support banking-system stability while informing the balance between financial innovation and prudential regulation.

title: The impact of top management team regulatory focus on accounting conservatism
summary: Purpose Drawing on regulatory focus theory, this study aims to examine how top management teams' (TMTs) motivational orientations (promotion versus prevention focus) influence accounting conservatism and further explores the internal and external situational conditions that shape this relationship. Design/methodology/approach Using textual analysis to quantify TMT regulatory focus from management discussion and analysis (MD&A) across Chinese A-listed firms, this study applies multivariate regression analysis to assess the impact of regulatory focus on accounting conservatism. Findings Our results show that promotion-focused TMTs are more likely to diminish accounting conservatism, whereas prevention-focused TMTs enhance it. TMT restricted stock (internal situational factor) attenuates both the negative effect of promotion focus and the positive effect of prevention focus on accounting conservatism. Analyst coverage (external situational factor) weakens the negative effect of promotion focus on conservatism while amplifying the positive effect of prevention focus. Further subgroup analyses reveal that the effects of TMT regulatory focus are more pronounced in non-SOEs and firms with lower ownership concentration and are significantly moderated by auditor industry expertise and product-market competition, highlighting the role of internal governance and external market factors as important boundary conditions. Originality/value This study introduces TMT regulatory focus as a novel psychological determinant of accounting conservatism, shifting the literature beyond observable demographic proxies to the motivational drivers of managerial reporting behavior. Furthermore, it identifies two actionable governance levers that interact with TMT motivational orientations, offering a more nuanced framework for corporate governance and compensation design.

title: Digital Transformation in Metallurgical Sector Logistics: A Case Study on the BPM Life Cycle of the Delivery Process Area
summary: The metallurgical sector faces significant logistic challenges to achieve efficient deliveries and increase customer satisfaction. This study analyzes and evaluates the application of the Business Process Management life cycle in the delivery process of a metallurgical company. Observation techniques, interviews, and surveys were used with clients as key actors in the process to evaluate the current logistics situation. Based on the evaluation outcomes, strategies and tools were identified to optimize planning, monitoring, and communication in the delivery process through the implementation of software for route optimization and order tracking in real time. Project management was developed under the Project Management Body of Knowledge methodological framework, which guaranteed efficient implementation and control. The results show significant improvements in operations and customer experience. This outcome emphasizes the importance of the digitalization of logistics to meet the specific demands and efficiency requirements of the metallurgical sector.

title: Measuring Business Value from Enterprise Analytics: Ethical Tensions, Valuation Frameworks, and Stakeholder Reconciliation
summary: The value of enterprise analytics has become a strategic necessity for today’s organizations, but the perception of business value is conceptually scattered and ethically debatable. The critical juncture between value measurement systems and ethical governance practices in enterprise analytics is explored through a comparison of purely financial return-on-investment (ROI) value frameworks and multi-stakeholder value frameworks, examining how they shape organizational decision-making and ethical outcomes. The study’s conceptual reconciliation process is grounded in a literature review of four key theories stakeholder theory, algorithmic fairness, integrated reporting, and data governance and identifies four fundamental ethical tensions: (1) shareholder primacy versus broader stakeholder equity; (2) short-term financial metrics versus long-term sustainability value; (3) algorithmic fairness versus analytical efficiency; and (4) opacity of data-driven decisions versus transparency obligations. The paper proposes a multi-dimensional value architecture combining financial performance indicators, environmental, social and governance (ESG) indicators, stakeholder participation mechanisms, and ethical audit procedures. The analysis suggests that organizations implementing stakeholder-inclusive analytics frameworks realize greater trust, innovation potential, and long-term resilience than those relying on financial ROI logic alone. The proposed framework is theoretically significant in extending stakeholder theory to the analytics domain, and practically significant in offering governance tools for reconciling conflicting value claims without compromising stakeholder rights or fairness. Policy implications for corporate governance boards and analytics practitioners are discussed.

title: From Accounting Records to Actionable Insights: Developing Business Analytics Capability in Small Enterprises
summary: Small enterprises may possess accounting records and digital dashboards without a reliable process for converting information into business decisions. This article examines that conversion through a focused narrative review of nine research and institutional sources concerning financial practices, analytics adoption, organisational capability and analytical reasoning. The synthesis distinguishes experimental effects from observational associations, policy evidence and stakeholder perceptions. It proposes an accounting to action framework linking a defined decision, dependable records, purpose appropriate analysis, understandable interpretation, documented action and subsequent review. The central proposition is that interpretation and review should be assessed alongside technology access: owners should be able to explain what an output supports, what it leaves uncertain and why a particular action follows. A worked hypothetical example demonstrates how revenue growth can coexist with a cash constraint. Implications for Bangladesh emphasise locally adapted instruction and evaluation rather than assumed transfer of foreign results. The framework is conceptual, not empirically validated. Its contribution is an operational account of how accounting discipline and learning routines can support business analytics, together with testable propositions and a design for evaluating decision quality separately from enterprise performance.Keywords: accounting information; business analytics; small enterprises; digital transformation; decision quality; Bangladesh

title: Does artificial intelligence improve social stability risk performance in China?
summary: This paper examines whether and how artificial intelligence (AI) contributes to improving the social stability risk level in China. Against the backdrop of rapid digital transformation and increasingly complex governance challenges, AI has been widely adopted in areas such as public security, social management, and risk monitoring. However, its actual effectiveness in mitigating social stability risks remains underexplored. Drawing on panel data from multiple regions in China, this study constructs an empirical framework to evaluate the impact of AI policy on social stability risk levels. The analysis integrates indicators of technological capacity, governance performance, and socio-economic conditions, and applies quantitative methods to identify both direct and indirect effects. The findings suggest that AI policy significantly reduces social stability risks by promoting digital economy development, increasing wage levels and investment in education. At the same time, the results reveal notable regional heterogeneity. The AI policy significantly reduces social stability risk in the central and western regions, and areas with moderate digital economy development, but has no statistically significant effect in economically developed and digitally advanced areas. The study also highlights potential challenges, including data governance concerns and uneven technological access, which may offset some of AI's benefits. This research contributes to the literature by linking technological innovation with social governance outcomes and provides policy implications for leveraging AI to promote social stability. It suggests that policymakers should not only invest in AI infrastructure but also address institutional and regional disparities to ensure inclusive and effective risk management.

title: Audit committee diversity as a moderator of the relationship between financial crises and firm profitability: evidence from the COVID-19 pandemic
summary: Purpose This study examines the moderating role of audit committee diversity in the nexus between financial crises (the COVID-19 crisis) and profitability. Design/methodology/approach This study analyses Jordanian non-financial companies listed on the Amman Stock Exchange as a sample for the study from 2018 to 2022. The hypotheses were tested using panel-corrected standard errors (PCSE) regression analysis to address the issues of heteroscedasticity and autocorrelation. This study uses the system Generalised Method of Moments (GMM), along with fixed-effects and dynamic regression analyses to address endogeneity concerns. Findings This paper concluded that the COVID-19 crisis negatively impacted the profitability of companies. Gender diversity moderated this relationship, significantly mitigating the negative impact of the pandemic, whereas the results did not indicate that nationality diversity played a moderating role. Practical implications This investigation relies on the novel results concerning the moderating effects of audit committee diversity characteristics, offering guidance to regulators on incorporating these underrepresented traits into corporate governance codes in Jordan and similar developing countries. Originality/value The literature investigating diversity’s influence on corporate profitability during crises predominantly emphasizes board-level diversity, direct impacts, and gender diversity. However, it often overlooks diversity within the audit committee and its effects when interacting with a crisis. To the author’s knowledge, this is the first study examining the moderating role of audit committee diversity (gender and nationality) in the association between the COVID-19 crisis and profitability in developing countries.

title: GENDER DIVERSITY IN TOP MANAGEMENT AND CORPORATE VALUE CREATION: EVIDENCE FROM CORPORATE BOARDS IN COLOMBIA.
summary: Background Gender diversity in corporate governance has gained increasing relevance due to regulatory changes, investor expectations, and its potential contribution to strategic decision-making and corporate value creation. Despite recent progress, women remain underrepresented on corporate boards. This study analyzes the relationship between female board participation and the financial performance of publicly traded companies in Colombia. Methods A quantitative, descriptive, and explanatory approach was employed. The study focused on Colombian publicly traded companies, particularly those included in the COLCAP index. Board composition and female participation were characterized using corporate and bibliographic sources, while financial and ESG data were obtained from LSEG and Refinitiv. Regression models examined the relationship between female board participation and financial performance, measured through ROA, and ROE, controlling for sales and ESG performance. Results Female participation on corporate boards increased substantially between 2015 and 2024, although significant differences remain across firms and sectors. The energy sector showed comparatively higher levels of female representation. Econometric results indicate a positive and statistically significant relationship between female board participation and ROE, with a correlation coefficient of 0.807 and a coefficient of determination of 65.1%, significant at the 1% level. These findings suggest that gender diversity is associated with improved corporate profitability. Conclusions Female participation on corporate boards is positively associated with financial performance, particularly ROE. Greater gender diversity may strengthen strategic decision-making and contribute to corporate value creation. However, persistent differences across firms and limited female representation in top governance positions indicate that further institutional and corporate efforts are required to achieve substantive gender equality.

title: Corporate Income Tax and Green Investment in Vietnam: Do Tax Incentives Really Generate Additionality?
summary: This study examines the relationship between corporate income tax, green investment, and ESG in Vietnam during the 2020–2025 period, drawing on a synthesis of domestic policy frameworks and international empirical evidence. The study focuses on whether tax incentives genuinely generate additional green investment or primarily reduce the tax liabilities associated with investments that firms would have undertaken anyway. The findings indicate that tax incentives can stimulate green investment by lowering after-tax costs and easing financial constraints; however, their effects are heterogeneous. Tax incentives may also give rise to non-additional investment, inefficient benefit allocation, and the risk of greenwashing. Against the backdrop of Vietnam’s ongoing efforts to refine its corporate income tax framework and green taxonomy, the study proposes a shift from incentives based predominantly on sectors or projects toward conditional, outcome-based incentives linked to additionality, measurable environmental outcomes, ESG transparency, and robust monitoring and clawback mechanisms. Accordingly, policy effectiveness should be assessed not merely by the amount of tax revenue forgone, but by the volume of additional green investment and the actual environmental outcomes generated per unit of foregone public revenue.

title: AI Washing and Stock Returns: Evidence from Chinese A-Share Firms
summary: Artificial intelligence has become increasingly prominent in corporate disclosure, yet firms' AI-related narratives may not always be supported by observable investment in technology or human capital. Using AI-related keywords from annual reports, AI patents, and AI-related job postings of Chinese A-share firms from 2020 to 2025, we construct a firm-year measure to examine this disclosure-investment gap. We classify a firm as an AI washer when its AI-related disclosure is above the industry-year median, while both AI patent activity and AI-related recruitment remain below their corresponding medians. Firms meeting this definition are associated with lower annual stock returns, and the result remains qualitatively unchanged when we use alternative methods to identify AI patents. Additional tests point to two related market responses: AI washing is accompanied by more negative media coverage and weaker investor sentiment. The return discount is also more pronounced among firms with higher institutional ownership and among firms in regions with stronger local AI policy support. These results suggest that investors do not treat AI-related disclosure independently of observable corporate activity. Instead, the impact of AI narratives on stock returns appears to depend partly on whether firms can support those narratives with technological development and hiring.

title: From pollution control to system governance: five decades of environmental policy evolution in China
summary: China's environmental governance has undergone a profound transformation since the late 1970s, with implications that extend far beyond its borders. Existing accounts of this evolution rely largely on qualitative periodisation and expert interpretation, offering limited capacity to trace long-term changes in policy priorities and governance logics. This study analyses 3460 central-level environmental policy documents from 1978 to 2025 through an integrated computational framework that combines large language model-based semantic enhancement, dynamic topic modelling, and multi-layer validation, measuring discursive intensity in both absolute and normalised terms across nearly five decades of policy development. The analysis traces five interlinked stages of environmental governance, marking a transition from problem-driven pollution control and energy conservation towards concept-led, system-oriented governance anchored in ecological civilisation and the dual-carbon agenda. Change across these stages is cumulative, not substitutive. Normalised measurement reveals a pattern of institutional persistence with declining relative dominance: foundational regulatory instruments grew in absolute frequency even as their share of policy attention fell, a signature of institutional layering in which new governance paradigms accumulate upon established foundations rather than replacing them. The trajectory of circular economy discourse, from peripheral mention in the 1980s to structural integration with carbon mitigation objectives, shows how resource conservation themes achieve institutional embedding within this evolving architecture. The study provides systematic, corpus-based quantitative evidence that confirms, refines, and extends established qualitative narratives, demonstrates a replicable framework for large-scale policy text analysis, and offers new insight into how state attention and governance paradigms evolve in rapidly transforming economies.

title: Compliance or Commitment? Hindustan Unilever's CSR Practice Under India's Mandatory CSR Regime, FY 2020-21 to FY 2024-25
summary: This paper examines Hindustan Unilever Limited’s (HUL) corporate social responsibility practice under Section 135 of India’s Companies Act, 2013. It uses a single-case design, drawing on HUL’s disclosed CSR financial data for FY 2020–21 to FY 2024–25, national CSR data, programme reports and peer-reviewed research. It examines how HUL’s spending compares with its statutory obligation, how its CSR is governed and connected to business strategy, what outcomes its flagship programmes report, and what limits CSR’s reach, particularly in relation to plastic packaging. Three findings emerge. First, HUL spent 2.01%–2.04% of average net profit on CSR in each year examined, close to the statutory 2% threshold; its CSR spending grew by about 54% over the period, largely alongside profit growth. Second, the case suggests a distinction between compliance in spending and commitment in programme design: initiatives such as Project Shakti and the Hindustan Unilever Foundation’s water programmes are linked to the company’s distribution and supply-chain context. However, the strength of evidence for reported outcomes varies, and company disclosures are not equivalent to independent impact evaluation. Third, plastic packaging highlights the limits of community CSR where impacts are tied to wider business operations and regulatory obligations. The paper argues that CSR should be assessed not only by expenditure but also by strategic integration, the strength of outcome evidence and transparency about limitations. It proposes a practical framework for measuring CSR performance beyond compliance reporting. Preprint; not peer-reviewed.

title: Overcoming Fragmented Plot Barriers: How Cultivated Land Concentration Advances China’s Agroecological Performance
summary: Reconciling grain production stability and agroecological sustainability is a key bottleneck for the high-quality development of China’s agriculture. As a critical form of cultivated land spatial restructuring, cultivated land concentration reshapes agricultural production and factor allocation, but whether it can break the long-standing trade-off between agricultural output growth and environmental protection remains unclear. Based on China’s prefecture-level panel data from 2000 to 2022, this study evaluates the impact of cultivated land concentration on agricultural green total factor productivity (AGTFP), identifies the underlying transmission channels, and assesses its spatial spillover effects. The results show that cultivated land concentration significantly improves AGTFP, and this green effect extends beyond local jurisdictions through positive spatial spillovers. The effect operates through the agglomeration of green finance and the development of agricultural production services. Heterogeneity analysis further shows that the effect is stronger in grain-dominated regions and weaker in highly mechanized areas. These findings contribute to reconciling national food security objectives with the long-term sustainability of China’s agroecosystems.

summary: The article provides a systematic critical analysis and a fundamental comprehensive assessment of the modern architecture of motivation models for top management of entities in the public sector of the economy of Ukraine in the context of macroeconomic instability, deepening structural transformations and challenges of post-war recovery. The specifics and dialectics of the functioning of compensation packages are analyzed in detail through the conceptual prism of the classical and neo-institutional theory of agency relations (Agency Theory), the concept of stakeholder capitalism (Stakeholder Capitalism). An analysis of European corporate governance practices is carried out (in particular, on the example of Equinor ASA, Norway). Based on the analysis, a comprehensive approach to adapting the best EU directives and recommendations to the domestic institutional landscape is developed, which forms a scientifically sound basis for reforming the strategic motivation of top management as a driver of the sustainability of the national economy. The key institutional and structural-organizational destructors of domestic corporate governance practice have been identified and systematically analyzed. In particular, the phenomenon of regulatory dualism in the public sector has been identified, which is caused by a constant regulatory gap between market requirements for attracting highly qualified leaders and strict directive restrictions on maximum remuneration levels (cap limits), fragmentation of corporate autonomy. A well-founded conclusion has been formulated that the public corporate sector is experiencing a critical devaluation and dysfunction of classical market instruments of long-term material incentives, which is due to strict regulation of the relevant relations. General conclusions are formulated based on the results of the study, in particular, the need for further implementation of OECD standards and EU directives (CSRD, CSDDD), which provide for the transition to a three-component remuneration structure with the dominance of long-term incentives (LTI), mandatory integration of non-financial ESG indicators, and legislative consolidation of bonus return mechanisms (Clawback), is substantiated.

title: Rethinking Growth in a Warming World: Sustainable Development Goals, Climate Policy and National Priorities
summary: The economy has always been considered one of the key pillars of national development and economic growth, higher production, industrialisation, infrastructure and consumption were considered as essential to improve the standard of living. But the speed of the climate change effects has made obvious the limits of the resource and carbon-intensive economic development models. The social and economic successes of more traditional development are under threat as the impacts of climate change-extreme weather events, biodiversity loss, water stress and economic disruption-grow more tangible with rising temperatures. The role of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) is in providing an integrated framework for balancing economic prosperity, social inclusion and environmental sustainability in this context. This article explores the need to reconsider traditional thinking about economic growth and climate change-focusing on the linkages between the SDGs, climate policy and national development priorities. It discusses the approaches to achieve Poverty Eradication, Job creation, Energy Security, Infrastructure Development, Climate Mitigation and Adaptation in the context of developing countries especially India. The article will also explore climate justice, sustainable finance, green growth, just transition and the structuring of legal and institutional frameworks for achieving sustainable development. It further suggests that we need to see climate action not as a limiting factor for economic development but rather as a chance to transform resources-intensive economic growth into economic growth that is resilient, resource efficient and inclusive. There is, therefore, a need to incorporate climate change into national planning in order to develop a growth model that ensures that future generations and those living in vulnerable areas can continue to enjoy developments.

title: Digital Customs and Vietnam's Logistics Competitiveness: From Procedural Electronification to Data Infrastructure
summary: In an international trading environment increasingly dependent on the speed, reliability, and predictability of supply chains, customs is no longer confined to the function of border control but is becoming a critical component of logistics data infrastructure. This paper examines the mechanisms through which digital customs affects logistics competitiveness, with a particular focus on Vietnam. A qualitative research approach is adopted, combining a synthesis and cross-examination of academic literature, policy analysis, descriptive statistics, and international comparisons. The findings indicate that the impact of digital customs does not derive simply from the electronification of procedures, but primarily from its capacity to reduce information frictions and uncertainty at the border. When data are standardized, interoperable, processed prior to the arrival of goods, and integrated with risk management, digital customs can shorten cargo release times, reduce compliance costs, and enhance the predictability and coordination of goods flows. In Vietnam, customs digitalization has made substantial progress; however, the measurement of its effectiveness should shift from the rate of procedural electronification toward tangible supply-chain outcomes. Accordingly, this study proposes treating digital customs as an integral component of national data infrastructure and evaluating its effectiveness through indicators encompassing time, stability, data reusability, risk management, and compliance costs.

title: Harnessing Dairy Goats for Food Security and Climate Resilience in Sub-Saharan Africa: An Interdisciplinary Review of Nutrition, Genomics, and Policy Pathways
summary: Dairy goats offer significant potential to enhance food security, promote climate resilience, and improve rural livelihoods in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), particularly within women-led smallholder farming systems. This interdisciplinary narrative review integrates findings from nutritional science, climate adaptation studies, recent genomic innovations, and policy analyses (2010–2025) to critically evaluate dairy goats’ roles in addressing persistent malnutrition and vulnerability to climate extremes. Goat milk provides vital macronutrients and micronutrients and can contribute to improved dietary adequacy. Compared with larger ruminants such as cattle, goats—particularly indigenous and locally adapted populations—often exhibit greater tolerance to heat stress, flexible browsing behaviour, and lower water requirements. However, these adaptive advantages vary widely among dairy goat breeds, with high-yielding temperate breeds generally showing lower resilience to climatic extremes than indigenous SSA ecotypes. In addition, the per-kg GHG emissions for goat milk are typically higher than those for bovine milk, although system-level benefits may emerge in drylands where goats fit local heat/feed constraints and where species mix and management differ substantially. Recent genomic advancements, notably genome-wide association studies and selection signature analyses, have identified candidate loci for thermotolerance, disease resistance, and milk yield. Near-term improvement is most plausible where breeding is anchored in community-based programmes supported by minimal identification and phenotyping, with marker use most defensible when validated within target populations. Despite emerging opportunities through microfinance and climate finance, especially for women-centric cooperatives, dairy goats remain underrepresented in national livestock and climate policies, and life cycle assessment data to support formal carbon–credit integration are limited. We therefore recommend dedicated funding to goat-specific extension and animal health, targeted gender-inclusive training, strategic investments in genomic and data infrastructure, and enhanced data collection for carbon accounting. Overall, the evidence synthesised here indicates that scalable dairy goat development in SSA is unlikely without the coordinated implementation of climate-smart management and delivery systems (animal identification and core recording), alongside context-validated genomic approaches (e.g., MAS or genomic prediction integrated within community-based breeding where reference resources and phenotypes exist) and targeted policy and financing.

title: Employee Readiness of PT EPN Towards Digital Transformation of Logistics Procurement and Its Impact on Supply Chain Visibility (SCV)
summary: Background: Digital transformation in logistics procurement depends strongly on employee readiness, particularly in organizations that are gradually introducing E-Procurement and the E-Vendor Management System (E-VMS) to replace manual procedures. Procurement activities involving vendors, internal units, and strategic partners require integrated digital support; however, evidence regarding employees’ preparedness for this transition and its consequences for Supply Chain Visibility (SCV) remains limited. Objective: This study examines employee readiness for digital transformation using the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) and evaluates its relationship with Supply Chain Visibility (SCV). Methods: An explanatory quantitative design was applied using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4. All 84 employees in the population were included through saturated sampling (census). Ten hypotheses were tested across Performance Expectancy (PE), Effort Expectancy (EE), Behavioral Intention (BI), Use Behavior (UB), and Supply Chain Visibility (SCV). Results: PE and EE positively affected BI, while PE and BI positively affected UB. UB was the strongest determinant of SCV. EE did not directly affect UB, and BI had no direct effect on SCV. BI fully mediated the effect of EE on UB, whereas UB mediated the effect of BI on SCV. Seven of the ten hypotheses were accepted, while three were rejected. Conclusion: Employee readiness was relatively favorable, but Supply Chain Visibility depended on actual system use rather than intention alone. Organizations should therefore ensure that employees’ usage intentions are translated into consistent use behavior so that digital transformation in logistics procurement can generate optimal benefits.

title: Digital Transformation, Carbon Disclosure, and Green Innovation in Energy Transition: Firm-Level Evidence from China’s Energy Sector
summary: China’s dual-carbon goals have made understanding how digital transformation shapes corporate carbon performance a policy priority, and the rapid expansion of firm-reported emissions disclosure since 2020 now makes such inquiry feasible at scale. Drawing on CSMAR financial data and CNRDS digital-transformation keyword frequencies for 914 A-share energy firms over 2020–2025, we combine panel fixed-effects models, a placebo-validated triple-difference design, disclosure-choice models with a Heckman selection correction, and event studies of two policy milestones. We find that digital transformation robustly stimulates green-patent applications and significantly raises the likelihood of carbon disclosure in the cross section, identifying green-patenting and disclosure as the two margins on which digitalization is already measurable. The direct association with disclosed carbon intensity remains statistically insignificant in the selection-corrected model and on the directly disclosed subsample, indicating that emission reductions are not yet measurable at the firm level. A sharp but short-lived emission-reduction pulse among digitalized high-carbon firms in 2021 is consistent with but does not confirm a Porter-type mechanism. Investors nonetheless priced transition-regulatory exposure: ETS-covered firms earned significantly negative abnormal returns around both policy milestones. Thus, digitalization in China’s energy sector is already visible in what firms invent and disclose, with measurable emission and valuation effects likely to follow as disclosure mandates and carbon pricing mature.

title: Neo-Banking Transformation: Institutional and Customer Readiness in Sri Lanka
summary: This study investigates the determinants of neo-banking adoption in Sri Lanka by integrating the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) with the Task-Technology Fit (TTF) model while examining the moderating role of perceived risk. A mixed-methods design was adopted, combining qualitative interviews with senior banking and fintech professionals and a survey of 200 banking customers. Quantitative data were analysed using PLS-SEM, while institutional insights were analysed through thematic analysis using NVivo. Results indicate that effort expectancy and task characteristics significantly influence behavioural intention, whereas performance expectancy, social influence, and facilitating conditions were insignificant. Perceived risk emerged as the strongest predictor and moderated the relationships with effort expectancy and task characteristics. The findings contribute to digital banking adoption literature by demonstrating how risk perceptions reshape technology adoption mechanisms in emerging economies. Practically, the study highlights the importance of user-centric design, regulatory clarity, and institutional readiness for successful neo-banking implementation.

title: THEORETICAL ASPECTS OF THE USE OF DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES IN THE ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT OF ENTERPRISES OF THE AGRO-INDUSTRIAL COMPLEX OF UKRAINE
summary: The relevance of the study is determined by the need to enhance the economic efficiency and sustainability of the enterprises within the agro-industrial complex of Ukraine in the context of digital transformation and increasing requirements for the performance of economic activity. The research is aimed to provide a scientific justification of the role of digital technologies in ensuring the economic development of agricultural enterprises and to identify the priority areas of digital transformation as well as economic mechanisms that contribute to improving efficiency, adaptability, and long-term stability. The article examines the current state and trends of digitalisation of agro-industrial enterprises in Ukraine, taking into account the level of their economic development under the influence of digital technologies. The economic impact of digital technologies on the operational efficiency of agro-industrial enterprises is analysed and substantiated. The role of digital technologies as a key factor in the economic development of the enterprises within the agro-industrial complex is determined. The priority directions for further digital transformation and economic mechanisms for ensuring the sustainable development of agro-industrial enterprises are identified. The research employs the methods of systems analysis, comparative and structural-functional analysis, generalisation of empirical data, and a review of contemporary scientific sources. The novelty of the study lies in a comprehensive approach to assessing the impact of digital technologies on the economic development of agro-industrial enterprises and in substantiating directions for their further transformation. The practical value of the article is reflected in the possibility of applying the proposed recommendations to enhance resource management efficiency, optimise business processes, and ensure the sustainable development of agricultural enterprises.

title: Fintech Development and Corporate Financial Policies: Evidence from Non-Financial Firms in the MENA Region
summary: This study examines the association between fintech development and corporate financing and investment policies among non-financial listed firms in ten MENA countries over 2010–2024. Using firm-level financial and market data together with country-year measures of fintech development, the analysis evaluates whether digital financial development is associated with firms’ external financing and investment activity. The baseline estimates indicate positive and statistically significant associations between fintech development and both external financing and corporate investment. Additional analyses examine heterogeneity related to information asymmetry, corporate governance, financial constraints, and ownership structure, as well as associations with the cost of debt, investment efficiency, and firm value. Robustness tests employ alternative fintech proxies and complementary specifications. The findings contribute to the literature by providing firm-level evidence from the MENA region and by documenting conditions under which the association between digital financial development and corporate financial policies varies. The results are interpreted as conditional associations rather than causal effects.

title: INTEGRAL UNDERSTANDING AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
summary: INTEGRAL UNDERSTANDING AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: Relational Architecture for Transduction, Memory, Discovery, Verification, and Mission Termination This research presents a relational and computational architecture for organizing artificial intelligence processes through transduction, structured state transitions, memory, search, verification, falsification, auditing, and explicit mission termination. The proposed architecture integrates a sequence of computational and epistemic operations: LATENCY → STRUCTURE → GENERATION → STATE → REFINEMENT → MEMORY → COVERAGE → BRANCHING → RECOVERY → REFUTATION → VERIFICATION → AUDITING → ARRIVAL CRITERION → STOP → RETURN → COCOON → END. The central objective is to establish a coherent framework in which the generation of candidate solutions is distinguished from their verification, the preservation of computational history, the recovery of previous states, and the determination of when a task has met its defined completion criteria. The article formalizes the architecture through a set of interacting components representing the state space, goals, actions, transition operators, memory, coverage, branching, recovery, refutation, verification, auditing, arrival criteria, and mission control. It also discusses potential applications to mathematical and computational research, software verification, cryptography, and the PAST-Mol computational hypothesis. Computational validation The study includes two computational experiments involving the Subset Sum problem. These experiments compare exhaustive enumeration with search strategies incorporating pruning and dynamic-programming guidance. Experiment 1 — Bound-based pruning For the set (A={1,2,\ldots,20}) and target (T=50), exhaustive enumeration examined (2^{20}=1,048,576) subsets and identified 1,969 solutions. A recursive search using upper-bound pruning visited 182,287 states and recovered the same 1,969 solutions. The reported reduction in the number of counted states was approximately 82.62%. Experiment 2 — Exhaustive search, pruning, and dynamic programming For a second set containing 20 positive integers and target (T=100), exhaustive enumeration, recursive bound-based pruning, and dynamic-programming-guided search each identified the same 51 solutions. The reported counts were 1,048,576 exhaustive masks, 19,763 states for bound-based search, and 1,455 search states for the dynamic-programming-guided strategy, with 2,121 dynamic-programming table cells. The search-state reduction relative to exhaustive enumeration was approximately 99.86% for the dynamic-programming-guided strategy. Both experiments report agreement between the solution sets and successful arithmetic audits. The results provide initial computational evidence for the tested search, pruning, and verification mechanisms. They do not, by themselves, establish a general polynomial-time algorithm, a universal efficiency guarantee, or a resolution of the P versus NP problem. The dynamic-programming result is understood in the context of the pseudo-polynomial dependence on the target value. Research contribution The principal contribution is the integration of computational search and epistemic control within a single relational architecture. The framework distinguishes candidate generation from verification, incorporates memory and recovery into the search process, and treats auditing and mission termination as explicit architectural functions rather than implicit outcomes. The two experiments provide an initial empirical basis for evaluating selected components of the proposal. Further research should extend the tests to larger and adversarial instances, measure runtime and memory under comparable conditions, conduct ablation studies, and compare the architecture against established algorithms and artificial-intelligence systems. The work is presented as a proposed architecture with initial computational validation and as a research program for developing more traceable, auditable, and systematically controlled computational processes.
