title: A Multi-State Linear Influence Model for Cyber Risk Propagation in Supply Chains
summary: Modern multi-echelon supply chains of critical infrastructure are increasingly defined by hyper-connectivity, driven by software integrations, cloud-based architectures, and enterprise resource planning synchronization. While these digital integrations optimize operational throughput, they simultaneously expose industrial networks to systemic, cascading cyber risks. Traditional supply chain risk management paradigms are often inadequate to capture the time-varying, multi-stage degradation characteristics of cyber threat propagation through the chain. This article introduces a baseline cyber risk propagation framework that couples a linear influence model (LIM) paradigm with a discrete 4-state operational security condition: Secure, Vulnerable, Compromised, and Offline. The proposed architecture leverages the additive and time-decaying properties of LIM frameworks to inherently resolve cyclic operational feedback loops while bypassing exponential state-space explosion. To operationalize the mathematical framework, we investigate four core resilience metrics: time-to-impact, area under the curve, cyber bullwhip effect, and recovery lag. Numerical simulations demonstrate the feasibility of this computationally tractable framework on synthetic networks, illustrating how it can be used to audit cascading propagation, evaluate containment strategies, and compare mitigation policies across multi-echelon ecosystems.

title: PENERAPAN FUNGSI DASAR MANAJEMEN PENDIDIKAN ISLAM DALAM MANAJEMEN BERBASIS TEKNOLOGI DI PESANTREN MODERN
summary: The digital transformation occurring within Islamic educational institutions requires a more adaptive and professional management system capable of meeting the demands for efficiency, accountability, and quality improvement. This study aims to analyze the implementation of fundamental Islamic educational management functions (POAC: Planning, Organizing, Actuating, Controlling) within a technology-based management system at Al-Ma'soem Islamic Boarding School, as well as to identify the challenges and opportunities emerging from this digitalization process. Employing a qualitative field-study design, data were collected through in-depth interviews, limited observations, and document analysis related to the digital management system. The findings indicate that planning, organizing, actuating, and controlling have been integrated through the use of management information systems, digital-competence-based staff recruitment, the utilization of digital administrative and learning applications, and monitoring mechanisms supported by dashboards and content-filtering systems. The results confirm that digitalization enhances the effectiveness of pesantren governance, although its success depends heavily on human resource readiness, infrastructure stability, and an organizational culture supportive of innovation. Theoretically, this study expands the discourse on Islamic educational management by offering the POAC-Digital concept, which integrates technological adaptation with Islamic values. Practically, the findings provide a strategic reference for developing modern pesantren management models that are more effective, accountable, and quality-oriented.

title: Impact of artificial intelligence on project planning, scheduling, and control
summary: Abstract The growing complexity of engineering and construction projects has revealed the weaknesses of conventional project planning, scheduling, and control approaches. Traditional tools often employ fixed assumptions, deterministic models, and past averages, which are inadequate for dealing with uncertainty, dynamic environments, and large-scale data. Artificial intelligence has become a disruptive technology that can be used to improve decision-making, prediction, and automation in project management processes. This paper examines the application of artificial intelligence in project planning, scheduling, and control within the engineering and construction sector. The paper summarises the application of artificial intelligence methods, including machine learning, optimization algorithms, and predictive analytics, in enhancing project performance using a methodical review of the recent scholarly literature and industry practise. The results show that artificial intelligence promotes the planning accuracy, flexibility of scheduling, and real-time project control to a great extent, as it allows data-driven insights and flexible responses. Issues of data quality, company preparedness, and ethical issues are major obstacles to implementation. The research paper adds to the project management literature because it develops the application of artificial intelligence in the three fundamental project management functions and provides practical advice to practitioners interested in introducing intelligent project management systems. title: Digital Marketing Capabilities, Innovation Capabilities, and Omnichannel Integration Quality on Digital Marketing Performance via Customer Value Co-creation: A Systematic Literature Review
summary: Digital transformation has fundamentally changed the marketing paradigm, moving organizations beyond simply delivering information toward technology-driven ecosystems that emphasize data, innovation, channel integration, and customer participation as important sources of value. This transformation requires organizations to develop digital capabilities that effectively connect technological resources with evolving customer needs. This study aims to synthesize existing literature on the relationships among Digital Marketing Capability, Innovation Capability, Omnichannel Integration Quality, Customer Value Co-Creation Behavior, and Digital Marketing Performance, while proposing a conceptual framework that explains how these constructs are interconnected. A Systematic Literature Review was conducted through several stages, including literature identification, selection, quality assessment, data extraction, and synthesis of findings from previous studies. Relevant literature was obtained from academic databases and search engines using combinations of keywords associated with Digital Marketing Capability, Innovation Capability, omnichannel integration, Customer Value Co-Creation, and marketing performance. The review primarily considered scholarly journal articles published from 2020 to 2026, complemented by seminal studies to establish construct definitions and theoretical foundations. The findings indicate that Digital Marketing Capability enables organizations to effectively combine technology, data, and marketing activities, while Innovation Capability supports the continuous development of services and processes. Meanwhile, Omnichannel Integration Quality contributes to a consistent and seamless customer experience. Together, these capabilities can encourage Customer Value Co-Creation Behavior, which functions as a key mechanism for improving Digital Marketing Performance. Grounded in Dynamic Capability Theory, the study proposes an integrative conceptual model and highlights future research opportunities, particularly in digital public services and utility platforms such as New PLN Mobile.

title: Corporate Governance Evidence from Strategic Emphasis: Evidence from India
summary: This study examines how corporate governance influences firms’ strategic emphasis following the adoption of takeover regulations in India. Specifically, it investigates whether a reduction in the threat of hostile takeovers affects the relative emphasis that firms place on short-term value appropriation and long-term value creation. Drawing on agency and stewardship perspectives, the study conceptualises advertising expenditure as an indicator of value appropriation and research and development (R&D) expenditure as an indicator of value creation. Using firm-level data from the Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy Prowess database for Indian firms over the period 2000–2024, this study examines changes in advertising and R&D intensity following the 2011 takeover regulation reform. The analysis employs panel-data techniques, including dynamic estimation, to assess the relationship between takeover-law adoption and firms’ strategic emphasis while accounting for firm- and industry-level characteristics. The findings indicate that weakening the threat of a hostile takeover is associated with greater emphasis on value appropriation, as reflected in advertising expenditure, providing support for the managerial-entrenchment perspective. In contrast, the evidence does not provide consistent support for the shareholder-interest perspective that reduced takeover pressure would encourage greater investment in long-term value creation through R&D. The findings suggest that changes in the corporate control environment can influence how managers allocate resources between immediate market-oriented activities and longer-term investments. The study contributes to the corporate governance literature by providing evidence from an emerging-market context and by highlighting strategic emphasis as an important mechanism through which takeover regulation may shape managerial resource-allocation decisions.

title: Strategi Kepemimpinan Transformasional Dalam Pengelolaan Perubahan Sumber Daya Manusia Di Era VUCA
summary: The VUCA era characterized by volatility, uncertainty, complexity, and ambiguity requires higher education institutions to develop adaptive capabilities in managing human resources. This study aims to analyze the implementation of transformational leadership in managing human resource changes at the Faculty of Social and Cultural Sciences, Universitas Pakuan. A qualitative case study approach was employed. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, observations, and documentation involving faculty leaders, department heads, lecturers, and administrative staff. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis through open coding, axial coding, and thematic interpretation. The findings indicate that transformational leadership significantly contributes to human resource change management through four dimensions: idealized influence, inspirational motivation, intellectual stimulation, and individualized consideration. Idealized influence and inspirational motivation strengthen organizational trust, commitment, and motivation toward change. Intellectual stimulation promotes innovation and digital transformation through the implementation of Learning Management Systems (LMS), although digital competency gaps remain evident. Meanwhile, individualized consideration requires further enhancement due to limited personalized approaches to individual needs. The study further reveals that human resource adaptability and organizational resilience serve as critical mechanisms in responding to VUCA challenges. The study proposes an Adaptive Transformational Leadership Model for the VUCA Era, illustrating the interaction among transformational leadership dimensions, human resource adaptability, and organizational resilience in supporting successful organizational change within higher education institutions

title: INDEPENDENT AUDITING: ADAPTATION PROCESS OF INDEPENDENT AUDITING STANDARDS AND THE EXAMPLE OF AZERBAIJAN
summary: This article examines how independent auditing standards are adapted to national systems, using Azerbaijan as a case study.Independent audits are essential for reliable financial reporting and investor confidence, yet international standards cannot be simply transplanted without regard to local legal and institutional realities.The central problem addressed is the gap that can arise between formal adoption of such standards and their effective implementation in practice.The study has two main purposes: to outline the core elements and stages of an effective adaptation process, and to assess Azerbaijan's experience in aligning its auditing framework with international benchmarks.Methodologically, the article relies on qualitative analysis of laws, regulations, professional guidance, and international assessments, complemented by academic literature and comparative insights.The findings show that Azerbaijan has made significant progress in translating and applying international standards, strengthening quality assurance, and upgrading professional education, particularly in key sectors such as banking and oil and gas.However, challenges remain in enforcement capacity, regional skills gaps, application to smaller entities, and ensuring auditor independence.The article concludes with policy recommendations and highlights avenues for future empirical and comparative research.

title: Beyond Digital Adoption: Mapping the Technological Transformation of State-Owned Television Broadcasting In Nigeria
summary: The study examines selected state-owned television stations in Nasarawa, Plateau and Benue States to determine whether digital adoption has translated into deeper technological integration and transformation, the creative application and organisational implications of digital technologies, and the institutional, infrastructural and human-capital conditions that shape this transition. The study draws on Diffusion of Innovation Theory and the Technology-Organisation-Environment (TOE) framework. The two theories allow the study to examine both how digital technologies are adopted and the organisational and environmental conditions that determine how deeply those technologies become integrated into broadcasting practice. The study adopted a cross-sectional survey design. The population comprised broadcasting personnel in the selected state broadcast stations, using convenience sampling based on accessibility and willingness to participate. The study found a high level of digital technology adoption and integration across the selected state-owned television stations. The study also found that digital technologies were creatively applied to programme development, editing, promotion, faster production, improved content quality, easier distribution, and staff adaptation. The study further identified challenges of funding, electricity, training, internet connectivity, and maintenance as constraints. And concluded that Digital transformation in state-owned television broadcasting extends beyond the acquisition of digital equipment. It depends on how effectively technology becomes embedded in everyday production, content development, distribution, and professional practice, and recommended that State-owned television broadcasters should move beyond equipment acquisition towards sustained technological integration, continuous professional development in daily digital operations, by creating opportunities for staff to experiment with new digital formats and production approaches.

title: The analytical study of strategic alliances, digital transformation, and relationship marketing in the pharmaceutical sector
summary: The relevance of the study is to substantiate the significance and development directions of strategic pharmaceutical alliances in the context of a combination of biological sciences, digital technologies, and new geopolitical conditions, as well as the European integration processes of domestic pharmaceutical enterprises and the need for foreign investment. Aim. To study, analyze, and generalize the features of strategic pharmaceutical alliances and their use of digital technologies and relationship marketing as innovative tools for developing and improving the competitiveness of pharmaceutical companies. Materials and methods. Scientific literature data, information websites of online publications, and pharmaceutical companies were used. The methods applied included the content analysis, system-analytical, structural-logical, grouping, and generalization methods. Results and discussion. The importance of strategic relationships at the international level has been shown; the features, advantages, possible problems and risks, as well as methods for mitigating them, and the future development prospects of pharmaceutical alliances have been identified. Attention is focused on the fact that the main goals of international strategic relationships in pharmacy are to solve problems of drug shortages and stabilize supply chains through harmonized regulatory frameworks and investment attraction. The role of digitalization and partnership relationships between pharmaceutical companies and digital platforms in the drug development and market promotion has been demonstrated. The advantages and forms of relationship marketing with examples from the pharmaceutical sector have been generalized. Conclusions. Strategic pharmaceutical alliances are one of the most effective and widespread forms of partnership that aligns with current trends in international cooperation and offers a significant potential for national pharmaceutical enterprises.

title: Advancing Sustainability through the Internet of Things (IoT) in Food Supply Chain Management: A Reflexive Thematic Analysis Approach
summary: Abstract: This study investigates how the Internet of Things (IoT) can advance sustainability within food supply chain management (SCM). The global food system faces pressing sustainability challenges including waste, inefficiency, and emissions. IoT technologies offer new opportunities to address these issues through enhanced visibility, resource optimisation, and data-driven decision-making. This research explores the role of IoT as a socio-technical enabler of sustainability, identifies adoption barriers, and interprets its integration within established sustainability frameworks. A qualitative research design grounded in Reflexive Thematic Analysis (RTA) was employed to analyse secondary data from academic studies, industry reports, and case examples. A hybrid deductive–inductive coding process was used, combining the Triple Bottom Line and Circular Economy frameworks with emerging patterns from the data. The study aligns its findings with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 2, SDG 9, SDG 12, and SDG 13. Four key themes emerged from the analysis: (1) IoT-driven efficiency gains, (2) transparency and traceability, (3) barriers to sustainable IoT adoption, and (4) IoT as a catalyst for sustainable transformation. IoT enhances operational efficiency, reduces resource waste, and promotes ethical sourcing through real-time data and automation. The study reveals IoT’s transformative potential when integrated with technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI) and blockchain to support circular and resilient food systems. The findings highlight strategies for cost-effective IoT implementation, cross-sector collaboration, and policy frameworks that strengthen digital infrastructure and governance. These insights support managers, policymakers, and technology providers in leveraging IoT for sustainable and inclusive food supply chains. This study contributes to the theoretical understanding of IoT as a socio-technical sustainability enabler, extending digital transformation research within the food sector. By applying reflexive thematic analysis, it provides a nuanced and integrative perspective on how IoT supports environmental, economic, and social goals simultaneously, offering a pathway towards achieving the SDGs and accelerating the transition to sustainable food systems. Keywords: Internet of Things (IoT), Food Supply Chain Management, Triple Bottom Line, Reflexive Thematic Analysis; SDGs; Digital Transformation

title: Farmers market as public quick commerce infrastructure: a conceptual policy framework for digital transformation
summary: The rapid digitalization of food retail through private quick commerce platforms has transformed urban food consumption patterns in India. Despite the investments in digital infrastructure, Uzhavar Sandhai (Farmers Market), a farmer-to-consumer direct marketing system in Tamil Nadu, is still limited to traditional physical markets. This study suggests a strategic rethinking of Farmers Market as a public quick commerce infrastructure layer, incorporating digital marketplaces, hyperlocal logistics and cooperative governance to boost farmer market competitiveness and promote public value, food system resilience and equitable digital market access. In this study, the Farmers Market Digital Platform model is developed by applying the conceptual policy design approach to convert the Farmers Market platform into a decentralized public quick commerce network. This study identifies the institutional, technological and governance reforms necessary to support the digital transformation of farmer markets using publicly governed digital infrastructure. This reorientation of Farmers Market to public digital infrastructure could form the policy roadmap for platformization of agriculture in Tamil Nadu, which would benefit small farmers, urban consumers, and municipalities and help alleviate inefficiencies in supply chains. As a conceptual policy framework, the proposed model has not been empirically tested and requires future pilot implementation and validation before adoption. The study contributes to the evolving literature on agricultural digitalization by offering a vision for the potential redesign of existing public agricultural markets as digitally enabled public service infrastructure, which can enhance farmer welfare and urban food system resilience.

summary: The article examines the theoretical and practical principles of the functioning of e-commerce enterprises in service markets under the conditions of digital transformation of the economy. The essence of service e-commerce is defined, its specific features are identified, and the main types of services that can act as independent objects of electronic purchase and sale are systematized. Particular attention is paid to the characteristics that distinguish e-commerce in services from electronic trade in tangible goods, including the intangibility of services, the simultaneity of production and consumption, the impossibility of storing unused capacity, personalization, the global nature of digital interaction, and the critical role of digital platforms. The study systematizes the main risks faced by e-commerce enterprises, including cyber, technological, legal, reputational, financial, competitive, marketing, and operational risks. The economic specificity of service e-commerce is associated with the combination of service intangibility, the decisive role of digital platforms as an environment for interaction, and a high level of information asymmetry between sellers and consumers. The importance of mechanisms for preliminary verification of service providers, standardization of service quality criteria and contractual conditions, payment and personal data protection, documentation of service delivery, guarantees, and alternative dispute resolution is substantiated. The study also emphasizes the importance of customer trust, transparency of digital transactions, and the availability of reliable feedback mechanisms, which directly affect consumer decision-making and the long-term sustainability of service providers in digital markets. It is concluded that the efficiency and competitiveness of e-commerce enterprises depend on their digital maturity, management quality, adaptability, and ability to implement innovative technologies. Further development is associated with artificial intelligence, business process automation, and the creation of integrated digital ecosystems.

title: Effect of Accruals Quality on the Firm Value of Construction and Allied Firms Listed at the Nairobi Securities Exchange, Kenya
summary: Accruals quality is a dimension of financial reporting quality because reliable accrual information enables investors to assess reported earnings and firm performance. However, evidence on whether accruals quality translates into higher firm value remains limited among construction and allied firms listed at the Nairobi Securities Exchange. The study examined the effect of accruals quality on firm value. It was anchored on Signalling Theory, which explains how credible financial information provides useful signals to market participants. A causal research design was adopted using panel data from four firms with financial information covering 2015–2025. Accruals quality was measured using the Dechow and Dichev (2002) model, while firm value was measured using Tobin’s Q. Panel regression analysis was conducted using STATA Version 18, with the hypothesis tested at the 5% significance level. The findings showed that accruals quality had a positive and statistically significant effect on firm value (β = 1.428, p = .003). This finding indicates that higher-quality accrual information was associated with higher market valuation among the sampled construction and allied firms. The study concluded that accruals quality was an important financial reporting attribute in explaining firm value within the sector. It recommended that firms strengthen accounting systems, internal controls, audit oversight, and financial reporting practices to improve the reliability of accrual information. Future research should examine whether audit quality, corporate governance, ownership structure, and investor information processing explain the relationship between accruals quality and firm value

title: Does corporate participation in rural revitalization improve carbon performance? Evidence fromknowledge resource integration and green innovation
summary: Purpose In the context of China’s “dual carbon” goals and the rural revitalization strategy, whether corporate social participation can translate into environmental benefits remains a critical yet underexplored question. Drawing on the knowledge-based view and organizational learning theory, this study aims to investigate whether and how corporate participation in rural revitalization improves corporate carbon performance. It further explores the mediating mechanisms of green innovation and financing constraint alleviation, as well as the moderating role of internal governance characteristics and external institutional environments. Design/methodology/approach This study utilizes a panel dataset of Chinese A-share listed firms from 2016 to 2021, comprising 1,016 listed companies and 5,513 unbalanced panel observations. Corporate carbon performance is measured using industry-level carbon emission data from the CEADs database, and rural revitalization participation is captured by both the logarithm of poverty alleviation fund investments and a dummy variable indicating whether a firm participates in rural revitalization. Fixed-effects models are employed to test the hypotheses, and a series of robustness checks – including replacing the dependent variable, propensity score matching (PSM), excluding carbon trading pilot cities and excluding municipalities directly under the central government – are conducted to address potential endogeneity concerns. Mediating effect models with bias-corrected bootstrap analysis (5,000 resamples) are used to examine the roles of green innovation and financing constraints. Heterogeneity analyses are further performed based on political connections, regional economic development levels and public environmental awareness. Findings The results show that corporate participation in rural revitalization significantly improves carbon performance. Mechanism analyses reveal that firms involved in rural revitalization are better able to acquire external knowledge resources, alleviate financing constraints and promote green innovation activities, thereby enhancing carbon performance. Specifically, green innovation and financing constraint alleviation serve as important partial mediating channels. Further heterogeneity analysis indicates that the positive effect is more pronounced among firms with politically connected executives, firms located in economically developed regions and firms facing higher public environmental scrutiny. Originality/value This study enriches the literature on corporate social responsibility and carbon management by integrating the knowledge-based view and organizational learning theory into the rural revitalization context. It provides novel empirical evidence on how rural revitalization participation drives low-carbon transformation through knowledge resource integration and green innovation, offering practical implications for policymakers and corporate managers seeking to achieve sustainable development and carbon reduction objectives.

title: ЕВОЛЮЦІЯ ТЕОРІЙ ІННОВАЦІЙНОГО МЕНЕДЖМЕНТУ
summary: The article provides a comprehensive examination of the evolution of theoretical approaches to innovation management and identifies the major directions in the transformation of its conceptual foundations under the influence of economic, technological, organizational, and societal changes. The relevance of the study is determined by the fact that, in an increasingly dynamic competitive environment, characterized by digital transformation, the spread of open innovation, the development of innovation ecosystems, platform-based business models, and artificial intelligence, traditional approaches to managing innovation activities require substantial reconsideration. The evolution of academic thought demonstrates a gradual shift from viewing innovation primarily as the outcome of a firm's internal research and technological development activities toward understanding it as a complex, systemic process of creating, disseminating, and commercializing new knowledge, technologies, products, services, processes, and business models involving multiple actors within an innovation ecosystem. he purpose of the study is to systematize and generalize the main stages in the evolution of innovation management theories, identify the underlying logic of the transformation of relevant theoretical paradigms, and substantiate the specific features of the contemporary stage of innovation management development, which is characterized by openness, ecosystem-based interaction, digitalization, the development of dynamic capabilities, and the use of artificial intelligence. The methodological foundation of the study comprises a combination of general scientific and specialized research methods. The historical and logical method was used to identify the sequence of formation and transformation of innovation management theories; the methods of analysis and synthesis were applied to systematize the principles of contemporary theoretical concepts; the comparative method was used to identify the common and distinctive characteristics of the principal paradigms; the systems approach was employed to examine the interrelationships between innovation strategy, resources, organizational capabilities, innovation processes, external partners, and ecosystems; and the generalization method was used to develop an integrated understanding of the contemporary innovation management model. The theoretical and informational basis of the study comprises recent academic works by international and Ukrainian scholars addressing innovation management, open innovation, dynamic capabilities, innovation ecosystems, digital technologies, business model innovation, and artificial intelligence. The scientific novelty of the study lies in systematizing the evolution of innovation management theories as a successive transition from resource- and technology-based and linear models to process-based, capability-based, open, ecosystem, digital, and human–AI hybrid paradigms. These concepts are interpreted not as mutually exclusive approaches, but as interconnected stages in the expansion of the subject matter and scope of innovation management. The study substantiates that the contemporary transformation of innovation management is manifested in a shift from managing individual innovation projects toward developing and enhancing a firm's innovation capabilities, managing knowledge and partnership networks, and orchestrating innovation ecosystems. It is demonstrated that digitalization and artificial intelligence constitute a qualitatively new stage in the development of innovation management theory, in which innovation processes increasingly take the form of human–machine hybrid systems. The study identifies the principal patterns underlying the development of theoretical approaches to innovation management. It is established that the initial focus on technological resources, research and development has gradually been complemented by process-based approaches, the concept of dynamic organizational capabilities, open innovation, innovation ecosystems, and digital transformation. The findings demonstrate that contemporary innovation management encompasses not only the creation of new products and technologies but also the management of knowledge, organizational change, business models, partnership networks, digital data, and intelligent technologies. The principal stages of theoretical evolution are systematized according to the object of management, sources of innovation, the role of the firm, and mechanisms of value creation. The study substantiates the need to integrate process-based, strategic, resource-based, network, ecosystem, and digital approaches into a contemporary innovation management model. It is established that the future development of innovation management theory is associated with the formation of responsible innovation management models, the integration of human and artificial intelligence, the development of digital innovation ecosystems, and the increasing importance of firms' dynamic capabilities. The findings can be used to further develop the theoretical and methodological foundations of innovation management, formulate innovation strategies, and design practical mechanisms for strengthening firms' innovation capabilities.

summary: The article substantiates the conceptual foundations for forming a digital security ecosystem in the tourism and hospitality industry. It is established that the digital transformation of tourism and hospitality enterprises and the spread of online booking platforms, mobile services, artificial intelligence, geographic information systems, the Internet of Things and cloud technologies simultaneously expand safety management capabilities and create new cyber, information, operational and reputational risks. The concept of a «digital security ecosystem in the tourism and hospitality industry» is clarified as an integrated human-centred environment for interaction among tourists, enterprises, digital platforms, public authorities, insurance and financial institutions, and emergency services, within which continuous data exchange, monitoring, forecasting, prevention, localisation and risk minimisation are ensured at all stages of the tourist journey. The main groups of threats are systematised, and the stakeholder, information, technological, functional and institutional components of the ecosystem are identified. The author’s Digital Security Ecosystem for Tourism and Hospitality (DSETH-model) is proposed, combining digital identification, data integration, risk monitoring, predictive analytics, communication, response and recovery. The principles of its functioning are substantiated: integration, interoperability, prevention, continuity, adaptability, cyber resilience, confidentiality, reliability, inclusiveness and accountability. The stages of practical ecosystem implementation and a set of indicators for assessing its effectiveness are determined. Particular attention is paid to the integration of digital technologies into a unified security environment capable of supporting proactive risk management and improving coordination among all stakeholders. The proposed conceptual framework may serve as a methodological basis for developing digital security strategies and implementing innovative management solutions in the tourism and hospitality industry. It is proved that applying an ecosystem approach will help reduce threat response time, increase consumer trust, strengthen the resilience of enterprises and tourism destinations, improve service quality and enhance the competitiveness of the tourism and hospitality industry.

title: The imprint of history: family firm origin and accounting information comparability in China
summary: Purpose Accounting information, serving as an important signal in capital markets, increasingly highlights the quality of financial reporting. This paper examines the differences in accounting information comparability across different family firm origins. Design/methodology/approach Using data on Chinese manufacturing family firms from 2009 to 2023, we employ a model with year and industry fixed effects to examine the relationship between family firm origin and accounting information comparability, as well as the underlying mechanisms. The final sample consists of 4,075 firm-year observations from 881 firms, with financial data obtained from the China Stock Market & Accounting Research database. Findings The main effects show that restructured family firms tend to have lower accounting comparability. The moderating effects show that the agency problem exacerbates this divergence in accounting comparability, whereas the number of generations involved in management mitigates it. The mechanism analysis shows that restructured family firms exhibit lower internal control quality and greater managerial myopia, both of which are associated with lower accounting comparability. Originality/value First, drawing on imprinting theory, this study finds that restructured family firms exhibit lower comparability of accounting information. This expands the scope of comparability research by extending it to factors related to historical origins. Second, this study expands upon the concepts of imprint dynamics and imprint decay in family firm origin research, thereby incorporating perspectives on the persistence and decay of imprints within imprinting theory. Finally, this paper adds a new dimension to research on the economic consequences of privatization for Chinese firms. Privatization not only affects operational efficiency but also shapes the information environment of financial reporting over the long term.

title: How leadership styles affect green supply chain management and innovation: the mediating role of green intellectual capital
summary: Purpose Green intellectual capital (GIC) and green leadership styles are vital strategic resources that enable firms to strengthen their sustainable competitive advantage by fostering environmental innovation and long-term value creation. This research presents a theoretical framework to examine the relationships among GIC components, green leadership styles, green supply chain management (GSCM), and green innovation (GI), grounded in the natural resource-based view and upper echelons theory. Design/methodology/approach This study employed a quantitative, cross-sectional survey design to examine the proposed relationships. Data were collected through an online questionnaire from 195 manufacturing firms across diverse industrial sectors in Türkiye. The proposed research model was evaluated using structural equation modeling (SEM) in Jamovi. Findings Our findings indicate that both green transactional and transformational leadership significantly and positively associated with the components of GIC. Specifically, green customer management has a strongly and positively associated with GI, whereas green supplier management shows no significant relationship with GI. Moreover, both green human capital (GHC) and green relational capital (GRC) partially mediate the relationship between green transformational leadership and GSCM (green supplier management and green customer management). Additionally, these dimensions partially mediate the relationship between green transactional leadership and green customer management and fully mediate the relationship between green transactional leadership and green supplier management. Originality/value This research contributes to the GSCM literature by integrating green leadership styles, GIC, and GI within a unified framework and examining the distinct roles of green human capital and green relational capital in the relationships between leadership and GSCM outcomes.

title: Digital transformation and SME innovation: The mediating role of financing constraints
summary: This study explores the impact of digital transformation on the innovation of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Based on 2018–2024 firm-level datasets, our results verify that digital transformation delivers remarkable promotional effects on SME innovation, improving innovation across both quantity and quality dimensions. From an economic perspective, a one-standard-deviation increase in digital transformation brings a 3.5% gain in innovation quantity and a 5.7% lift in innovation quality. Specifically, digital transformation fosters more patent applications and grants, and also increases the technological value of patents. Financing constraints are found to partially mediate the relationship under investigation. Digital transformation can alleviate information asymmetry, enhance the credibility of enterprises, and thus alleviate financing constraints and promote more continuous innovation activities. Further heterogeneity analysis shows that the positive effect of digital transformation on innovation is significantly stronger for non-state-owned enterprises (non-SOEs) than for state-owned enterprises (SOEs) in terms of ownership. This could be because non-SOEs are more market-sensitive and have stronger incentives to transform. As for regional heterogeneity, digital transformation has a significant effect on promoting innovation in the eastern region, and also exerts a positive effect in the west, with a stronger marginal impact. This study builds theoretical bases and implementable guidance for enterprises, regulators, and financial lenders, helping SMEs overcome innovation challenges and encouraging the digital and real economies to become more deeply intertwined.

title: How digital workplace conditions shape career adaptability: the mediating role of job satisfaction
summary: Purpose Drawing on self-determination theory (SDT) and career construction theory (CCT), this study examines whether and how digital workplace conditions influence employees' career adaptability through job satisfaction in Vietnam's technology sector. Specifically, it proposes that employees' positive evaluative experience of digitally enabled work, reflected in job satisfaction, serves as the psychological mechanism through which digital workplace conditions translate into adaptive career resources that support effective functioning in digital work settings. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted with 312 employees working in technology firms in Hanoi, Vietnam. Data were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) to assess measurement validity and to test the proposed direct and indirect relationships among the constructs. Findings The results reveal that digital work environment factors - namely technology readiness, digital leadership, organisational culture, and task–technology fit - have significant and positive effects on job satisfaction. Job satisfaction, in turn, significantly enhances employees' career adaptability. Moreover, the indirect effects of all four digital workplace conditions on career adaptability through job satisfaction are significant, thereby confirming the mediating role of job satisfaction and suggesting that supportive digital workplace conditions enhance career adaptability by fostering more positive evaluations of digitally enabled work. Practical implications The findings suggest that organisations should approach digital transformation not only as a technology implementation issue but also as a people-and-performance challenge. In practice, managers should prioritise improving task–technology fit and building a supportive digital culture, while strengthening employees' technology readiness and leaders' day-to-day digital support. Job satisfaction can also be used as an early diagnostic indicator of whether digital workplace conditions are enabling employee adjustment and career adaptability. Originality/value This study advances theory by conceptualising the digital workplace as an integrated socio-technical system shaping employees' career adaptability through people-related processes. By integrating SDT and CCT, it identifies job satisfaction as a key psychological mechanism linking digital workplace conditions to career adaptability. Empirical evidence from Vietnam's technology sector further extends existing knowledge beyond Western contexts and highlights the critical role of motivationally supportive digital work environments in developing employee adaptability relevant to organisational effectiveness.

title: Metaverse and immersive technologies in supply chain management and operations: A systematic review of research trends, theories, and future directions
summary: The metaverse and related immersive technologies are increasingly discussed as enablers of digital transformation in supply chain management and operations (SCM&O), yet the research base has not been systematically mapped. This study reviews how the field has developed, which research approaches and theories it uses, and where future research is needed. A systematic literature review was conducted on Scopus for the period 1996 to 2025, following the protocols of Tranfield and colleagues and the PRISMA framework. Thirty eight peer reviewed articles in ABDC listed journals (ratings A*, A, and B) were selected using predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, and VOSviewer was used for complementary bibliometric analysis. Publication activity was sporadic before 2020 and peaked in 2023, with contributions concentrated in the United States, the United Kingdom, and India. Conceptual studies (10), systematic reviews (7), analytical and mathematical modelling (7), and mixed methods studies (6) dominate, while case based and quantitative studies are scarce. Thirty one of the 38 studies (81.6 percent) report no explicit theoretical foundation, and game theory and the technology organization environment framework are the only theories used more than once. The synthesis identifies seven research directions: theory development, empirical and methodological strengthening, geographic and sectoral expansion, technology integration, sustainability and resilience, governance, security and trust, and human and organizational dimensions. The findings should be read with caution because the search used a single database and a journal rating filter.

title: Reconceptualizing green innovation as an organizational capability: an integrated approach
summary: Purpose This paper reconceptualizes green innovation as an integrative organizational capability rather than a standalone environmental or technological initiative. It examines how organizational, institutional and technological conditions shape its contribution to sustainable organizational performance. Design/methodology/approach The paper adopts a narrative literature review, drawing on the natural resource-based view (NRBV) to synthesize research on organizational capabilities, organizational learning, stakeholder relationships, institutional conditions and digital technologies. Findings The review shows that green innovation contributes to sustainable performance when supported by complementary capabilities, organizational learning, stakeholder collaboration, favorable institutional conditions and digital technologies. It further suggests that technologies alone are insufficient; outcomes depend on aligning organizational capabilities with contextual conditions. Research limitations/implications As a conceptual review, the proposed framework requires empirical validation across different organizational and institutional contexts. Practical implications Managers should embed green innovation within organizational strategy, strengthen learning, strengthen stakeholder collaboration, leverage digital technologies and adopt context-specific sustainability strategies. Originality/value The paper advances an integrative capability-based perspective by positioning green innovation capability as the mechanism through which organizational resources, learning, stakeholder relationships, institutional conditions and digital technologies are combined to generate sustainable performance.

title: Rebirth amidst risk: can the digital economy break the urban resource curse? evidence from resource-based cities
summary: Digital transformation reshapes global economic paradigms and offers a pathway for resource-dependent regions to transcend the “resource curse.” By leveraging panel data from 111 Chinese resource-based cities between 2011 and 2019, this study empirically examines whether the burgeoning digital economy facilitates departure from resource-dependent stagnation. First, our analysis validates the presence of a robust resource curse within the sample, and subsequently scrutinizes the moderating role of digital development. The results reveal that (1) the digital economy significantly and sustainably mitigates the resource-growth paradox. (2) This moderating influence exhibits pronounced heterogeneity, contingent on the city’s geographical location and the specific stage of resource exploitation. (3) The efficacy of digital interventions is nonlinear and varies across thresholds of digital maturity. These findings underscore the strategic importance of digital infrastructure in fostering economic resilience and provide critical policy insights for regions seeking to decouple their growth trajectories from finite natural resources. Digital transformation is emerging as a critical pathway for resource-dependent regions seeking to overcome the “resource curse” and build more resilient growth models. This study examines 111 Chinese resource-based cities and assesses whether digital development can weaken the adverse relationship between resource dependence and economic growth. It finds that the digital economy significantly and persistently mitigates the resource curse, while revealing substantial heterogeneity across geographical locations and stages of resource exploitation. The analysis further uncovers a nonlinear relationship, showing that the effectiveness of digital interventions changes as cities cross different thresholds of digital maturity. These findings reframe digitalization as more than a general growth engine: it is a context-dependent mechanism for reducing resource dependence and facilitating structural transformation, providing actionable evidence for designing differentiated digital development strategies in resource-based regions.

title: From Export Gatekeeping to Sustainability Finance? Palm Oil Trade Governance, Smallholder Compliance, and Indonesia’s Economic Diplomacy in the EUDR Era
summary: Indonesia’s palm-oil sector is entering a regulatory transition in which export governance, smallholder sustainability, and external market access are becoming increasingly interconnected. This qualitative literature review examines whether centralized palm-oil export governance could evolve beyond trade administration into an institutional platform for sustainability finance and stronger economic-diplomatic credibility. Drawing on more than 50 peer-reviewed journal articles published during 2020–2026, the review integrates scholarship on deforestation-free supply chains, the European Union Deforestation Regulation (EUDR), sustainability certification, independent smallholders, replanting, agricultural finance, traceability, state-influenced commodity marketing, and trade–environment relations. Seven interconnected findings emerge: sustainability obligations are moving upstream; smallholder exclusion reflects structural rather than merely technical constraints; replanting involves a combined productivity and income-transition problem; centralized export governance can create a financing node but not automatically additional finance; financial and institutional support are complementary; verifiable domestic compliance may contribute to external credibility; and concentrated trade governance may introduce liquidity, transaction, competition, data, and accountability risks. The review develops an integrated trade finance compliance diplomacy framework and argues that export-linked sustainability finance is conditional on transparent additionality, smallholder accessibility, land legality, interoperable traceability, institutional separation of commercial and financing functions, and independent monitoring. The article concludes with an agenda for evaluating Indonesia’s emerging export architecture empirically after implementation.

title: Pengaruh Good Corporate Governance, Sistem Pengendalian Internal, dan Ukuran Perusahaan terhadap Financial Statement Fraud pada Perusahaan Consumer Good di BEI 2020-2025
summary: The incongruity of prior findings concerning the role of Good Corporate Governance and the firm-specific attributes of companies in the consumer goods industry during the 2020–2025 period provides the impetus for investigating the determinants of Financial Statement Fraud. This study examines consumer goods companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange to ascertain the association of Good Corporate Governance, Internal Control Systems, and Firm Size with Financial Statement Fraud. The dataset comprises annual reports, audited financial statements, and Good Corporate Governance reports from 15 companies selected through purposive sampling, yielding 90 observations over a six-year observation period. Financial Statement Fraud is proxied by the Dechow F-Score, while GCG is operationalized through independent commissioners, audit committees, and institutional ownership; Internal Control Systems are measured through disclosed internal control components; and Firm Size is gauged by the natural logarithm of total assets. Statistical evidence of a significant association with Financial Statement Fraud emerges solely for Firm Size, which exhibits a negative relationship with a significance value of 0.012, whereas GCG and Internal Control Systems demonstrate no statistically significant effects, with respective significance values of 0.912 and 0.637. These findings indicate that the GCG and internal control indicators employed in this study lack sufficient statistical explanatory power to account for variations in Financial Statement Fraud, whereas an expansion in firm scale is associated with a diminished propensity for financial statement fraud.

title: Analisis Faktor Penyebab Fraud dalam Perbankan Syariah : Perspektif Good Corporate Governance dan Etika Islam
summary: Penelitian ini membahas faktor penyebab fraud dalam perbankan syariah di Indonesia dengan meninjau dua perspektif utama, yaitu Good Corporate Governance (GCG) dan nilai-nilai etika Islam. Fraud dalam perbankan syariah tidak hanya dipengaruhi oleh kelemahan pengendalian internal, tetapi juga erat kaitannya dengan lemahnya penerapan prinsip moral dan etika Islami dalam praktik sehari-hari. GCG berperan penting dalam mengurangi potensi fraud melalui mekanisme pengawasan, transparansi, independensi dewan, serta efektivitas audit internal. Sementara itu, etika Islam memberikan landasan moral yang mendorong terciptanya budaya kerja yang amanah, jujur, dan bertanggung jawab. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode literatur review dengan menelaah hasil-hasil penelitian terdahulu berupa jurnal, artikel ilmiah, dan buku nasional yang terbit dalam lima tahun terakhir. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa integrasi antara GCG dan etika Islam dapat menjadi strategi efektif dalam mencegah maupun meminimalisasi fraud di sektor perbankan syariah. Dengan demikian, penelitian ini diharapkan dapat memberikan kontribusi bagi pengembangan sistem pengendalian yang tidak hanya berbasis regulasi formal, tetapi juga pada penguatan nilai moral Islami.

title: ANALYSIS AND EVALUATION OF BANK PRODUCTS AND SERVICES IN AZERBAIJAN AND IN THE WORLD IN THE MODERN ERA
summary: The banking sector in Azerbaijan has undergone significant transformations, especially after the country gained independence.The regulatory framework is largely governed by the Central Bank of Azerbaijan, which has been shaping policies on interest rates, credit policies, and foreign exchange regulations.Currently, the major banks in Azerbaijan include both state-owned and private institutions that play a crucial role in the economy by providing essential banking services like savings accounts, personal loans, mortgages, and credit cards.On the global stage, banking services have increasingly shifted towards digitalization, with many customers opting for mobile banking, internet banking, and fintech solutions.Globally, the trend has also moved towards sustainability, with banks introducing green financing and socially responsible investment products, considering environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors.With financial markets becoming more interconnected, Azerbaijan's banking system is starting to align with global financial frameworks, although there are still gaps in terms of offering advanced products and services compared to more developed markets.In Azerbaijan, traditional banking products are widely offered, but there is a growing shift towards innovative financial services, including digital banking platforms and contactless payment systems.The customer experience in Azerbaijan is steadily improving, although banks need to enhance accessibility, transparency, and reduce fees to keep pace with global customer expectations.

title: Predicting ESG adoption among Malaysian SMEs using explainable machine learning
summary: Abstract Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) considerations are increasingly embedded in regulatory frameworks, financial markets, and corporate strategy worldwide. While large listed firms have been the primary focus of ESG reporting requirements, small and medium enterprises (SMEs) play a central role in employment, supply chains, and regional development, particularly in emerging economies. In Malaysia, SMEs account for the vast majority of business establishments, yet ESG adoption remains uneven across firms. This study examines which non-practice firm-level characteristics are associated with ESG adoption classification among formal-sector Malaysian SMEs using explainable machine learning. The sample of 457 firms is drawn from a bank-linked stakeholder network, so it over-represents formal-sector, bank-connected SMEs, and the outcome is self-declared. The survey records ESG adoption on a four-level scale (fully, partially, planning to, or not implementing), which is recoded into a binary adopter/non-adopter target for the main analysis; it reflects reported adoption status rather than a verified measure of ESG performance. Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, and Explainable Boosting Machine (EBM) are compared using nested cross-validation with all preprocessing fitted inside the cross-validation pipeline. On the held-out test set of 92 observations, Random Forest recorded the highest discrimination point estimates (ROC-AUC = 0.853; adopter-positive PR-AUC = 0.904). Paired bootstrap comparisons showed higher Random Forest discrimination than XGBoost and EBM, but did not distinguish Random Forest from Logistic Regression on ROC-AUC. No model was uniformly superior across all reported metrics, and the estimates remain imprecise because of the small held-out sample. On a common measure of variable-level importance computed for all four models, several predictors recur near the top, most consistently the use of financial consultants as an ESG advisory source, ownership type, and company type or market orientation, followed by programme-awareness and funding-intent variables. When the models are refitted across cross-validation folds, the rankings shift and few variables hold a fixed position, so these are reported as recurring but unstable predictive signals rather than a stable set of determinants. The results are predictive and non-causal: the model identifies firm characteristics associated with higher predicted adoption probability, not causal mechanisms. Performance is evaluated internally, with no external validation, so the model is exploratory and not ready for operational allocation or policy deployment. Within that scope, the findings offer an interpretable basis for exploratory segmentation of formal-sector, bank-connected SMEs and may help generate hypotheses for more targeted sustainability support.

title: Decision-Making in Power Supply Chains Considering Natural Hazards
summary: Natural hazards have a significant impact on the power supply chain and simultaneously affect the utilization efficiency of renewable energy. The joint effect of disaster probability and emergency procurement costs on pricing, renewable energy investment, and profit distribution within a two-echelon power supply chain remains underexplored. To fill this gap, we construct two game-theoretic models: Model S in a stable natural environment and Model D under natural hazards. The main conclusions are as follows: (1) In both scenarios, the profit level of the producer depends on the probability of natural hazards. When 0 < μ ≤ μ1, the producer earns a higher profit in Model S, whereas when μ1 < μ < 1, the producer earns a higher profit in Model D. The profit level of retailers depends on the unit procurement price of emergency supplies and the probability of natural hazards. (2) In a stable natural environment, the optimal wholesale price set by the power producer, the optimal retail price set by the electricity retailer, the demand for renewable energy electricity, the total electricity demand, and consumer surplus are all higher than in the scenario where a natural hazard occurs. In the scenario of a natural hazard, the profit of the players is determined by the proportion of renewable energy power supply and prevailing market demand conditions. (3) As the preference coefficient for renewable electricity increases, the retail price, electricity demand, profit of both players, and consumer surplus all rise. In contrast, the renewable energy investment cost coefficient has the opposite effect on them. Additionally, the demand for traditional energy power is positively correlated with the investment cost coefficient.

title: Institutional Quality and the Financial Returns of Social Supply Chain Practices
summary: ABSTRACT Social supply chain practices (SSCP) have become increasingly relevant as firms seek to support sustainable development and respond to stakeholder expectations. This study examines the association between SSCP and corporate financial performance (CFP) and investigates the moderating role of country‐level institutional quality. Drawing on resource dependence, legitimacy, and institutional theories, we constructed a composite SSCP index based on 11 binary indicators and applied fixed‐effects panel regressions to global firm‐level data from 2018 to 2023. The results show that SSCP is negatively associated with return on assets (ROA) and Tobin's Q , while their association with market capitalization is not statistically significant. The interaction between SSCP and country‐level institutional quality is positive and significant across all three CFP measures, indicating that the estimated SSCP–CFP association becomes more favorable as institutional quality increases. However, the conditional pattern differs across the three CFP measures. For market capitalization, the association becomes positive and statistically significant at high levels of institutional quality, whereas for ROA and Tobin's Q , it becomes statistically indistinguishable from zero and does not become significantly positive within the observed range. Thus, by combining a social‐specific measure of supply chain practices, multiple dimensions of CFP, and country‐level institutional quality in a global sample, this study provides a more integrated examination of the SSCP–CFP association. These findings show that the SSCP–CFP association varies across financial measures and institutional governance contexts, highlighting country‐level institutional quality as an important boundary condition in this association.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN ACCOUNTING AND AUDITING: TRANSFORMING FINANCIAL DECISION-MAKING AND PROFESSIONAL PRACTICES
summary: Abstract: The emergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has significantly transformed accounting and auditing practices across organizations worldwide. The increasing availability of financial data, advancements in machine learning algorithms, and the demand for real-time financial information have accelerated the adoption of AI-driven technologies in accounting and auditing functions. Traditional accounting systems primarily relied on manual data processing and periodic reporting, whereas AI enables continuous monitoring, predictive analytics, automated transaction processing, and intelligent decision support. In auditing, AI enhances fraud detection, risk assessment, anomaly identification, and audit quality through automated analysis of large volumes of structured and unstructured financial data. The integration of technologies such as Machine Learning (ML), Natural Language Processing (NLP), Robotic Process Automation (RPA), and Generative AI has redefined professional roles and transformed the manner in which financial information is generated, analyzed, and interpreted. Despite numerous benefits, the adoption of AI also raises concerns regarding data privacy, algorithmic bias, transparency, ethical accountability, and workforce readiness. This paper examines the role of AI in accounting and auditing, explores its influence on financial decision-making, evaluates its benefits and challenges, and discusses future implications for accounting professionals. The study is conceptual in nature and is based on an extensive review of recent academic literature and professional reports. The findings indicate that AI acts as an enabler of enhanced efficiency, accuracy, and strategic decision-making while complementing rather than replacing human expertise in accounting and auditing.

title: The Effect of Relational Resources on Supply Chain Robustness: The Moderating Role of Relational Capital
summary: Increasing supply chain disruptions have intensified the need for firms to develop capabilities that support operational continuity and effective responses to uncertainty. Although previous studies have examined supply chain robustness through operational and technological perspectives, limited attention has been given to how relational resources influence robustness and how relational capital shapes these relationships. This study examines the effects of resource complementarity and resource specificity on supply chain robustness and investigates the direct and moderating roles of relational capital among firms in the Greater Accra Region of Ghana. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted using structured questionnaires administered to supply chain managers. Of the 384 questionnaires distributed, 296 valid responses were used for analysis. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) was performed using SmartPLS. Resource complementarity positively influenced supply chain robustness (β = 0.714, p < 0.001), whereas resource specificity had a significant negative association with robustness (β = −0.305, p = 0.022). Relational capital had a positive direct effect on robustness (β = 0.618, p < 0.001). It also positively moderated the relationship between resource complementarity and robustness (β = 0.292, p < 0.001) and negatively moderated the relationship between resource specificity and robustness (β = −0.197, p = 0.012). The study concludes that relational resources contribute significantly to supply chain robustness, but their effects depend on the nature of the resources and the relational conditions surrounding their use. Firms should strengthen collaboration and combine complementary partner resources while managing relationship-specific investments carefully to avoid unnecessary constraints on operational flexibility.

title: Green Finance, Executive Corruption, and Inclusive Green Growth in Developing Countries
summary: Despite growing international commitments to green finance, it remains an open empirical question whether such transfers translate into inclusive green growth (IGG) in developing countries. This study addresses this gap by examining how countries’ levels of development and executive corruption condition the effects of green finance on IGG. The empirical analysis draws on a comprehensive sample of 99 developing countries from 2000–2024 and employs instrumentalvariable and quantile regression techniques. Our findings show that green finance promotes IGG only in low-income countries, with the largest gains accruing to those with the lowest IGG performance. However, executive corruption significantly undermines these gains, nullifying the positive effect of green finance at a threshold of 0.6. These findings suggest that executive corruption can transform green finance from a driver of IGG into an impediment as fragilities in the institutional fabric for controlling executive corruption deepen.

title: Industry 4.0 technologies and environmental sustainability performance in supply chains: an exploratory statistical and machine learning analysis
summary: Purpose This study examines how key Industry 4.0 technologies relate to environmental sustainability performance in supply chains. Specifically, it examines Internet of Things, Artificial Intelligence, Big Data Analytics, Blockchain, Digital Twin and Cloud Computing, and explores their relative associations with sustainability outcomes using both statistical and machine learning techniques. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was adopted. Data were collected from 268 supply chain and logistics professionals across multiple industries. Descriptive and inferential statistical analyses were conducted using SPSS software version 31.0.2. Machine learning analysis was carried out using Orange Data Mining to perform feature importance ranking and decision tree modeling, with model performance evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation. Findings Correlation and hierarchical regression analyses reveal no statistically significant association between any individual Industry 4.0 technology and environmental sustainability performance and tested pairwise interaction effects are likewise non-significant. Exploratory machine learning feature rankings order the technologies differently across three methods, and cross-validated models do not outperform a mean-only baseline, indicating no detectable predictive signal in these data. Research limitations/implications The study is based on cross-sectional survey data, which limits causal interpretation and does not capture changes in technology adoption and sustainability performance over time. The sample, although adequate for the applied analyses, is restricted to 268 respondents and may not fully represent all industries and geographical contexts. Future research should use longitudinal designs, larger international samples and additional Industry 4.0 technologies to extend the understanding of digital transformation and sustainability relationships in supply chains. Practical implications The findings caution against expecting sustainability improvements from technology adoption alone. No individual technology, and no tested combination, showed a statistically significant association with environmental sustainability performance, and cross-validated models showed no predictive signal. The results redirect managerial attention from technology acquisition toward the mediating organizational practices through which digital technologies may generate sustainability value. Originality/value This study measures six Industry 4.0 technologies as separate constructs within a single sample, combines conventional statistical testing with exploratory, cross-validated machine learning, and transparently reports a null result for direct technology–performance associations a finding that complements prior mediation-based evidence by suggesting that direct effects of individual technologies may be weak in the absence of mediating capabilities.

title: The Moderating Effect of Audit Quality on the Relationship Between Internal Controls and Financial Reporting Quality of Non-Financial Companies Listed at The Nairobi Securities Exchange, Kenya
summary: This study examined whether audit quality moderates the relationship between internal control systems and financial reporting quality among non-financial companies listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE). Although internal controls are intended to support reliable reporting, their contribution may depend on the strength of external audit scrutiny. Using a positivist, quantitative explanatory longitudinal panel design, the study analysed secondary data from 26 non-financial firms over 2010–2025 (416 firm-year observations). Internal control systems were assessed through an Internal Control Disclosure Index (ICDI) based on the five COSO components. Audit quality was represented by a composite index incorporating auditor size, audit tenure and audit opinion; the use of audit opinion as an outcome-related indicator is a measurement limitation that should be considered when interpreting the index. Financial reporting quality was proxied by signed discretionary accruals estimated using the modified Jones model and reverse-coded so that values closer to zero indicated higher quality. The study used firm fixed-effects regressions with firm-clustered robust standard errors to estimate direct and interaction effects. The interaction between internal control systems and audit quality was positive and statistically significant (? = 1.038, p = .013), providing evidence that the association between internal controls and reporting quality varies with audit quality. The result supports rejection of the null hypothesis of no moderation, although it should be interpreted as an estimated conditional association rather than proof of causation. The study contributes Kenya-specific panel evidence on the complementary roles of internal controls and external audit in financial reporting governance.

title: CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY (CSR) DALAM KAITANNYA DENGAN PELESTARIAN LINGKUNGAN DAN MASYARAKAT WILAYAH PESISIR DAN PULAU-PULAU KECIL DI INDONESIA
summary: Wilayah pesisir dan pulau-pulau kecil di Indonesia memiliki potensi sumber daya alam yang melimpah, namun sekaligus sangat rentan terhadap degradasi lingkungan dan masalah ketimpangan sosial-ekonomi. Kehadiran berbagai aktivitas industri dan korporasi di sekitar kawasan ini membawa dampak ekologis dan sosial yang signifikan, sehingga menuntut optimalisasi pelaksanaan Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR). Artikel ini bertujuan untuk mengkaji dan menganalisis implementasi program CSR dalam kaitannya dengan pelestarian lingkungan serta pemberdayaan masyarakat di kawasan pesisir dan pulau-pulau kecil Indonesia. Melalui metode kualitatif dengan pendekatan studi literatur dan analisis deskriptif, penelitian ini mengevaluasi berbagai praktik CSR yang telah berjalan. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa sebagian besar implementasi CSR di wilayah ini masih cenderung bersifat karitatif (bantuan sesaat) dan belum sepenuhnya berorientasi pada keberlanjutan. Tantangan utama yang dihadapi meliputi minimnya partisipasi masyarakat lokal dalam perencanaan, ketidaksesuaian program dengan karakteristik geografis pulau kecil, serta kurangnya sinergi dengan pemerintah daerah. Program CSR dinilai efektif apabila mengintegrasikan kearifan lokal dan pendekatan ekonomi sirkular, seperti program rehabilitasi ekosistem mangrove, budidaya perikanan berkelanjutan, dan pengembangan ekowisata. Disimpulkan bahwa CSR di wilayah pesisir dan pulau-pulau kecil harus bertransformasi dari kewajiban filantropis menjadi strategi penciptaan nilai bersama (Creating Shared Value). Diperlukan kolaborasi sinergis antara perusahaan, pemerintah, dan masyarakat untuk mewujudkan kelestarian ekologi pesisir yang selaras dengan peningkatan kesejahteraan nelayan dan penduduk setempat.

title: Value Relevance of Earnings, Book Value and Operating Cash Flows: Evidence from Listed Industrial Goods Companies in Nigeria
summary: This study examined the relationship between value relevance of earnings, book value and operating cash flows: evidence from listed industrial goods companies in Nigeria over the period 2015–2024. The study adopted an ex-post facto research design and utilised a balanced panel dataset comprising 120 firm-year observations from 12 listed industrial goods companies selected from a population of 15 firms on the Nigerian Exchange. Market Price Per Share (MPS) was used as the proxy for market value, while Earnings Per Share (EPS), Book Value Per Share (BVPS), and Cash Flow from Operations Per Share (CFFO) were examined as accounting information variables, with firm size included as a control variable. Data was obtained from audited annual reports, financial statements, NGX publications, company websites, and Securities and Exchange Commission records. The data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation analysis, diagnostic tests, and panel regression techniques using EViews. The descriptive results revealed substantial variations in market prices and accounting information across the sampled firms. Correlation analysis showed strong positive relationships between MPS and EPS (r = 0.8789), CFFO (r = 0.8701), and BVPS (r = 0.8189), while firm size exhibited a moderate positive correlation with MPS (r = 0.6123). The findings provide preliminary evidence that accounting information is relevant to the market valuation of listed industrial goods companies in Nigeria. The study recommends improved quality, transparency, and timeliness of financial reporting to enhance the usefulness of accounting information to investors and other capital-market participants.
